16.59: So, this is what the Lord Yahweh says, “When you abrogated the covenant you made with me, you showed no respect for your solemn promises. I will deal with you as these actions deserve. \
16.60: Yet I myself will uphold and fulfill the solemn promise that I made with you when you were young. Yes, I will make a promise with you that will never end.
16.61: Then you will recall what you once did and feel humiliating shame when you reconcile with your sisters, both those older than you and those younger than you. I will present them to you as your daughters, but not because of my covenant with you. \
16.62: So I myself will make my solemn promise with you. When this happens, you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God!
16.63: I will do this so that you will recognize all that you have done and feel ashamed. When I forgive you for all that you have done and restore our relationship, your disgrace will cause you to never again open your mouth to speak.” This is what the Lord Yahweh declares!’” \

17.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
17.2: “Human, tell this ambiguous story to the Israelite people.
17.3: Tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “There once was a huge eagle with powerful wings and long feathers of many colors. It flew to Lebanon and grasped the top of a cedar tree.
17.4: It broke off the topmost of its young branches and carried it away to the Canaanite territories. The eagle set it down in a city of vendors. \
17.5: Then it took some of the seed of that land and planted it in a fertile field, in a slip beside abundant water. He planted it there like one plants a willow tree.
17.6: That seed sprouted and became a low, spreading vine. Its tendrils grew toward the eagle, and its roots extended down beneath it. So it became a vine that produced woody branches and put out canes. \
17.7: There was another huge eagle with powerful wings and many feathers. Now, the spreading vine bent its roots toward this second eagle. From the garden bed where it grew, the vine stretched out its tendrils toward the eagle, hoping that it would give the vine more water.
17.8: The first eagle had planted the vine-plant in a fertile field that ran along flowing water so that it could grow woody canes and produce fruit and become a splendid vine.”’ \
17.9: Then say, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “This vine will clearly not flourish! Someone will rip up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it wilts and dies. All its fresh new leaves will wilt and die. ( And it will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots!)
17.10: Now, consider this: Even though the eagle planted it, it will clearly not flourish! When the hot east wind blows on it, it will entirely wither and die. Yes, it will wither away, right in the garden bed where it once grew.”’” \
17.11: Then Yahweh gave me this message:
17.12: “Ask those Israelite people who continually revolt against me, ‘You do not understand what this ambiguous story means, do you?’ Tell them, ‘Remember: The Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem, captured the Judahite king Jehoiachin and his public officials, and brought them back to himself in Babylon. \
17.13: Then he took one of the royal family — Jehoiachin’s uncle, Zedekiah — and made a royal treaty with him, coercing him to swear a solemn oath. He also forcibly removed the most powerful local rulers of Jerusalem,
17.14: so that the Judahite kingdom would remain weak and unable to revolt against him. Instead, it could survive only by honoring its treaty with the Babylonian king, Nebuchadnezzar. \
17.15: However, the man whom the Babylonian king set up, Zedekiah, revolted against Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian Empire. Zedekiah dispatched his messengers to Egypt, to Pharoah Hophra, so that the Egyptian Empire would equip him with horses and many soldiers. Clearly, Zedekiah will not flourish! He who does such things will certainly not survive! Zedekiah disregarded the treaty he made with the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar, so he will clearly not survive!
17.16: I swear by my own life that Zedekiah will die in Babylon, in the city of the king who made him king, whose oath he disregarded and whose treaty he violated. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare! \
17.17: Hophra, the king of Egypt, will not employ his massive army to fight alongside Zedekiah in the battle when the Babylonian Empire constructs a siege ramp and erects siege walls to kill many people.
17.18: Zedekiah, the so-called king of Judah, showed no respect for his oath to Nebuchadnezzar and broke the treaty he had made. Make note: He made a solemn promise, yet he did all these things. So, he will clearly not survive! \
17.19: So, this is what the Lord Yahweh says, “I swear by my own life that the oath to Nebuchadnezzar that Zedekiah disregarded, he swore in my name! And the covenant he violated was with me! I will repay him for these actions!
17.20: I will ensnare Zedekiah and capture him, like an animal that a hunter traps with a net. I will forcibly bring him to Babylon, and there I will legally arraign him for disloyally betraying his promises to me.
17.21: With their swords, Babylonian soldiers will murder every one of Zedekiah’s soldiers who flees in the battle, and those who survive will disperse in every direction. When all this happens, you will recognize that I, Yahweh, have spoken!” \
17.22: This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “I myself will remove a shoot from the top of a tall cedar tree, and I will plant it. I will break off a newly grown, green twig from the topmost of its young shoots, and I myself will plant it on a towering mountain.
17.23: I will plant that newly grown green twig on the highest mountain of Israel, where it will grow woody branches and bear fruit and become a magnificent, wide cedar tree. Birds of every kind will nest under it; every kind of winged animal will live in the shade of its branches. \
17.24: Then every tree in the field will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God! I fell tall trees and cause small trees to grow tall; I dry up green trees and make dry trees flourish. I am Yahweh — I have spoken, and I will certainly do it!”’” \

18.1: Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
18.2: “What do you people mean when you quote this proverb about the land of Israel? You say, ‘The parents ate sour grapes, but it was their children who got the sour taste in their mouths.’ \
18.3: I swear by my own life that you, Israelite people, will no longer quote that proverb in Israel. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare!
18.4: Pay attention! All lives are mine — parents and their children alike. It is the person who sins who will die. \
18.5: Suppose there is a virtuous person who does what is just and honest.
18.6: He does not eat meat that people have sacrificed to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops, nor does he pray to the idols that the Israelite people worship. He does not defile another man’ s wife, nor does he have sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period of menstruation. \
18.7: He does not extort anyone. When he borrows money from someone and the person gives him something as collateral for repayment, he gives that item back to the lender. He does not steal from anyone. Instead, he gives his food to hungry people and gives his clothing to people who have no clothes. \
18.8: When he lends someone money, he does not charge interest or engage in usury. He refuses to do what is immoral or corrupt. Instead, he judges honestly between one person and another.
18.9: He carefully acts according to my regulations and lives faithfully by heeding my norms. In this case, people should consider this person righteous. He will surely continue to live! That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
18.10: But suppose that such a virtuous man has a violent son, who murders people. Then that son does any of these evil things to other people —
18.11: all the things that his father never did: He eats meat that people have sacrificed to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops; he defiles another man’s wife. \
18.12: He extorts people who are poor and helpless. He steals from people, and, when he borrows money from someone and the person gives him something as collateral for repayment, he refuses to return that item to the lender. He prays to the idols that the Israelite people worship and commits other disgusting and illicit things.
18.13: When he lends someone money, he charges interest and engages in usury. Such a person will surely not go on living! Because he has done all these disgusting and illicit things, people must execute him and hold him responsible for his own death. \
18.14: But pay attention! Suppose that such a violent man has a son who witnesses all the sins that his father commits, considers them, but does not do such things.
18.15: He does not eat meat that people have sacrificed to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops, nor does he pray to the idols that the Israelite people worship. He does not defile another man’s wife; \
18.16: He does not extort anyone. When he borrows money from someone and the person gives him something as collateral for repayment, he gives that item back to the lender. He does not steal from anyone. Instead, he gives his food to hungry people and gives his clothing to people who have no clothes.
18.17: He refuses to do what is immoral or corrupt. When he lends someone money, he does not charge interest or engage in usury. He lives in a way that heeds my norms and carefully acts according to my regulations. In this case, such a person will not die because of his father’s sins; he will surely go on living! \
18.18: But as for his father, pay attention! He will die because of his own depraved behavior. After all, he extorted people, stole from his relatives, and generally did what is wrong among his people. \
18.19: But you retort, ‘Why would the virtuous son not suffer for the wrong that his father did?’ I answer: The son has done what is just and honest and has carefully lived his life according to all my regulations. For this reason, he will surely go on living!
18.20: The person who sins is the one who will die. A son will not suffer what his father’s corrupt actions deserve, nor will a father suffer what his son’s corrupt actions deserve. Righteous people will enjoy the consequences of their righteous behavior, and wicked people will suffer the inevitable outcomes of their wicked behavior. \
18.21: But suppose that a wicked person stops doing all the sinful things that he once did and begins to carefully live his life according to all my regulations and do what is just and honest. If this happens, this once-wicked person will surely go on living! I will not put him to death.
18.22: I, Yahweh, will not treat him according to any of the rebellious things that he once did. Instead, he will go on living because of the virtuous things that he now does. \
18.23: Indeed, I do not enjoy it when wicked people die. I do not want them to die! That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. So, when they stop behaving wickedly, they will go on living. \
18.24: But suppose a virtuous person stops doing what is just and honest and begins to behave corruptly and to do the same disgusting things that wicked people do. That formerly virtuous person will certainly not go on living! I will not credit him for the just and honest things that he once did. Instead, he will die because he has disloyally betrayed his promises to me and has committed many sins. \
18.25: But you retort, ‘The Lord’s conduct is not fair!’ Listen to this, you Israelite people: It is not what I do that is unfair; rather, it is what you do that is unfair!
18.26: If a righteous person stops doing what is right and honest and commits sins, he will die because of the sins that he committed. \
18.27: But if a wicked person stops doing wicked things and does what is just and honest, he will save his own life.
18.28: Because he witnessed all his sinful actions and stopped revolting against me, he will surely go on living; he will not die. \
18.29: But you people of Israel say, ‘The Lord does not act fairly.’ You people of Israel, it is not my ways that are unfair; rather, it is your ways that are unfair.
18.30: Therefore, Israelite people, I, Yahweh, will judge each one of you according to what you have done. Repent, and stop all your rebellious behavior, so that your sins will not cause you to die! This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare! \
18.31: Stop revolting against me. Remove your rebellious behavior as if it were garbage to throw away! Change the way you think and the way you live. Israelite people, there is no reason for you to die!
18.32: I do not enjoy it when any person must die! So repent so that you might live! This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare!” \

19.1: Yahweh said to me, “Lament over the ruling officials of Israel.
19.2: Say this to the Israelite people, ‘Imagine — your mother was such a lioness; she lay herself among male lions and bore more and more cubs surrounded by young, virile lions.
19.3: She reared one of her cubs until he was a virile lion, teaching him to hunt and kill wild animals; he even learned to kill and eat people!
19.4: When people from other people groups learned about him, they captured him in a pit. They put hooks on him and dragged him away to Egypt. \
19.5: The young lion’s mother waited for him to return, but she was utterly disappointed when he never came back. So she reared another one of her cubs, and made him into another virile lion.
19.6: He prowled among the other lions, and he too became a virile lion. He learned to hunt and kill wild animals, and he even killed and ate people!
19.7: He consorted with his widows, and he razed cities into ruins. When he roared, everyone who lived in the land ran away. \
19.8: But then people from the surrounding people groups arrayed themselves against from every province. They spread their net over him; they trapped him in a pit.
19.9: They shut him in a cage, They put hooks on him and dragged him away to the king of Babylon. They locked him in a prison so that the people on the mountains of Israel would never again hear him roar. \
19.10: Imagine —your mother was like a flourishing, verdant vine that somebody planted beside flowing water. Because there was plenty of water, she had many canes and produced many grapes.
19.11: It had strong, woody branches, suitable to become a ruler’s scepter. It towered high overhead, into the very clouds, and people could see how tall it was and how full it had become. \
19.12: However, Yahweh became so angry that he pulled the vine up by its roots and flung it down to the ground. A hot east wind dried up its fruit, The vine’s strong branches broke off; they dried up, and a fire burned them up.
19.13: Now, Yahweh has transplanted that vine —your mother — in a desert, in a dry and arid region. \
19.14: A fire has spread out from the stem of its shoot, which has burned up all its fruit. So now, no strong branch remains on it — no branch that could become a ruler’s scepter.’ This is a lament, and people will indeed sing it to grieve for the Israelite people.” \

20.1: In the seventh year after the Babylonians forcibly removed King Jehoiachin and the many other peoples of Jerusalem and relocated them to Babylon — on the tenth day of the fifth month — some of the Israelite elders came to inquire of Yahweh what they should do. So, they sat down in front of me. \
20.2: Then Yahweh gave me this message. He said,
20.3: “Human, speak to the Israelite elders and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “So you have come to inquire of me what you should do! I swear by my own life that I refuse to let you ask me anything.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.’ \
20.4: Human, you must announce my judgment against those elders! Yes, you must pronounce my judgment! Make them acknowledge the disgusting and illicit things that their ancestors did.
20.5: Tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘When I chose your ancestors to be my people, I solemnly swore an oath to the descendants of Jacob. While they lived as slaves in Egypt, I demonstrated to them who I am. I solemnly swore to them that my name was Yahweh, and that I was their God.
20.6: At that same time, I solemnly promised them that I would bring them out of the Egyptian territories into a land that I had selected for them. The soil in that land was very fertile and produced good crops abundantly — it was the most beautiful of all lands. \
20.7: I said to them, “Every one of you must discard the abhorrent idols that attract your attention! You must not make yourselves ritually unfit to worship me by revering the ritual statues that the Egyptians worship! I am Yahweh your God!” \
20.8: But they revolted against me and refused to obey me. Not one of them discarded the abhorrent idols that attracted their attention and devotion, nor did they desert the ritual statues that the Egyptians worshiped. So I declared that I would completely vent my furious anger against them — right there in the Egyptian territories.
20.9: But I did not do this, because I wanted to preserve my reputation. I did not want the people groups among whom my people were living to think little of me. They had witnessed me disclose myself to my people when I brought them out of the Egyptian territories. \
20.10: So I brought them out of the Egyptian territories and led them into the desert wilderness.
20.11: I told them how they ought to live, and I taught them my norms. Anyone who heeds these things will live because of them!
20.12: I also gave them the day of my Sabbath rest. I intended those days to remind them that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. I set them apart to belong to me. \
20.13: But the Israelite people revolted against me in the wilderness. They ignored my instructions and refused to live by my norms, even though anyone who heeds these things will live because of them! They also completely dishonored my Sabbath days. So I declared that I would completely destroy my people by venting my furious anger against them in the desert wilderness.
20.14: But I did not do this because I wanted to preserve my reputation. I did not want the people groups who witnessed it when I brought Israel out of Egypt to think little of me. \
20.15: I also solemnly swore to them in the desert wilderness that I would not bring them into the land that I had given them. The soil in that land was very fertile and produced good crops abundantly — it was the most beautiful of all lands.
20.16: I swore this because they ignored my instructions, refused to live by my norms, and dishonored my Sabbath days. After all, they deeply desired to worship their ritual statues.
20.17: But I had compassion on them and did not kill every Israelite person; I did not completely destroy them in the desert wilderness. \
20.18: I said to the children of the Israelite people who had died in the wilderness, “Do not live by the instructions that your parents followed; do not heed their norms, and do not make yourselves ritually unable to worship me by honoring your parents’ ritual statues.
20.19: Remember: I am Yahweh your God. Live according to my instructions; carefully heed my norms and do them!
20.20: Honor my Sabbath days as holy, so that they remind you that I, Yahweh your God, am the all-powerful God!” \
20.21: But their children also revolted against me. They ignored my instructions and refused to live by my norms, even though anyone who heeds these things will live because of them! They also completely dishonored my Sabbath days. So I declared that I would completely vent my furious anger against them in the desert wilderness.
20.22: But I held back from punishing them and did not carry out my intent to destroy them, because I wanted to preserve my reputation. I did not want the people groups who witnessed it when I brought Israel out of Egypt to think little of me. \
20.23: I also solemnly swore to them in the desert wilderness that I would scatter them among other people groups and countries.
20.24: I did this because the Israelite people ignored my instructions, refused to live by my norms, completely dishonored my Sabbath days, and focused their devoted attention on the ritual statues that their ancestors worshiped. \
20.25: So I permitted them to follow instructions that were not good for them and norms by which they could not preserve their lives.
20.26: I let them defile themselves by the sacrifices they offered to other gods when they ritually burned their firstborn children alive. I did that in order to devastate them, so that they would that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.”’ \
20.27: Therefore, human, tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “Here is yet another way that your ancestors insulted me! They were disloyal and betrayed their promises to me.
20.28: I led them into the land that I had solemnly promised to give to them. But whenever they saw a hill or a verdant tree, they offered their sacrifices to other gods there. At those places, they presented offerings to the other gods that angered me, burning aromatics that gave off a pleasing smell and pouring out their wine offerings.
20.29: So I asked them, ‘What is this high place that you keep going to?’” ( To this day, people call such places Bamah, a name that means ‘high place.’)’ \
20.30: Therefore, tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “You are making yourselves ritually unfit to worship me in the same way that your ancestors did! Likewise, you are being unfaithful to me by worshiping the detestable idols that they worshiped!
20.31: You presented your ritual gifts to the gods and burned your children alive! When you worshiped the other gods this way, you made yourselves unfit to worship me! And you are still doing these things today! So I will certainly not let you ask me for advice, you people of Israel. I swear by my own life that I refuse to let you ask me anything.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.
20.32: “What you are thinking will never happen. You say to yourselves, ‘We want to become like the other people groups, like the empires of other lands, who worship ritual statues that they have crafted from wood and stone.’” \
20.33: This is what the Lord Yahweh declares, “I swear by my own life that I will powerfully rule over you. I will show you how furiously angry I am!
20.34: I will powerfully lead you out from among the foreign people groups and collect you from the territories where I scattered you. And I will show you how furiously angry I am!
20.35: I will lead you into a desert wilderness that lies among the other nations, and there, I will personally arraign you. \
20.36: I will legally arraign you just as I did with your ancestors in the desert wilderness near the land of Egypt.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares!
20.37: “I will count each one of you, like sheep passing under a shepherd’s staff, and I will require you to honor the covenant that I made with you.
20.38: I will expel from among you those who revolt against me and disobey me. I will lead them out of the territories where they have been living as foreigners, but they will never enter the land of Israel. Then you will finally know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God!” \
20.39: As for you, people of Israel, this is what the Lord Yahweh says, “If you refuse to listen to me, then go ahead and keep worshiping your idols, every one of you! But you will never again dishonor me, the holy God by offering your gifts to your idols. \
20.40: Because this is what the Lord Yahweh declares, “On my holy mountain, Zion, Israel’s lofty mountain, all the people of Israel, every one of them, will worship me there in the Israelite territories. There, I will accept them, and there I will require them to bring me their ritual contributions, the firstfruits of their tributes, along with all their holy sacrifices and offerings.
20.41: When I smell your aromatic sacrifices, I will reconcile myself with you. I will lead you out from among the foreign peoples and gather you from the territories among which I scattered you. Then, the nations will witness what I do among you and will recognize that I am holy. \
20.42: You will finally understand that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I solemnly swore to give to your ancestors.
20.43: In that land, you will remember how you formerly behaved and everything you did that made you ritually unfit to worship me. As a result, you will despise yourselves for all the corrupt, wicked things that you did.
20.44: You will understand that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God when I act mercifully toward you to protect my reputation, and not according to what your wicked and corrupt behavior deserves, you people of Israel.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.’” \
20.45: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

20.47: Tell them about that forested part of the Negeb, ‘Listen to the message that Yahweh is sending you! He says, “Pay attention! I, the Lord Yahweh, am about to start a fire in you, and it will ignite every tree in the Negeb, both the verdant trees and the dry ones. No one will put out that blazing fire, and it will scorch every part of the land — from the south to the north. \
20.48: Then everyone alive will see that I, Yahweh, started that fire. No one will ever put it out.”’”
20.49: Then I said, “Oh, Lord Yahweh! People are dismissing me by saying, ‘He is only speaking in figures of speech!’” \

21.1: Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
21.2: “Human, turn and face toward Jerusalem. Speak out an ecstatic prophetic message against the temple there, and declare what I have to say about the people who live in the land of Israel.
21.3: Tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what Yahweh has to say, “Pay attention! I have become your enemy! I am about to send a warring army against you, and it will kill both the righteous people and the wicked people among you. \
21.4: Yes, I am going to kill both righteous people and wicked people among you. As a result, I will send that army against everyone who lives in the land of Israel — from its southernmost parts to its far north.
21.5: Then everyone will understand that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. It was I who sent that army, and I will not call it back until it has finished.’” \
21.6: So then, as for you, human — exclaim an audible groan of your deep sorrow! Groan in anguish and bitter grief while the people of Israel are watching you.
21.7: They will ask you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ And you must answer, ‘I am groaning because of the news that I have heard about what is about to happen. When other people learn of it, all of them will lose their courage; they will become dismayed and terrified, and they will urinate themselves. Pay attention! 21.8: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
21.9: “Human, declare my message! Tell the people that this is what I, the Lord, say, ‘I see a sword! A sword! Someone has sharpened it and polished it. \
21.10: He sharpened it in order to slay many people; he polished it so that it gleams brightly, as if it were lightning! The royal scepter of my son Judah has no reason to celebrate! This sword will cut down every kingdom, as one cuts down a tree!
21.11: The sword’s owner polished it so that a warrior could grip the sword in his hand. He sharpened and polished it, in order to give it to the man who will use it to kill. \
21.12: Human, mourn and loudly weep! After all, this sword will attack my people and all the local officials of Israel! I have decided that my people and their leaders will die by that sword. So slap your hand against your thigh to show how horrified you are.
21.13: I am putting my people to the test, and the sword will destroy the king of Judah, who shuns my warnings. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’ \
21.14: So then, you human, speak my messages, and clap your hands together to show that I have decided to punish them. Let that sword strike them once more — even a third time! That sword kills people; it is a sword that slaughters great numbers of them, closing in on them from every side. \
21.15: I am doing this so that they will lose their courage and so that many of them will fall over and die. At every city gate, I have stationed soldiers with pointed blades. How terrible this is! Someone made that sword to flash about as it strikes; the soldiers will pull out their swords to massacre people with them.
21.16: Go on, soldiers! Slash your swords to the right! Again! Slash them to the left! Thrust your swords wherever your sword’s edge happens to go!
21.17: Even I myself will clap my hands to announce that I have finished judging them, and then I will no longer be angry. This will assuredly happen because I, Yahweh, have said it would!” \
21.18: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
21.19: “As for you, human, draw a map on which you have mapped out two routes for the army of the king of Babylon to march along. Both routes must start out from the same territory. Then, fashion a signpost and place it at the place where each route turns toward a major city.
21.20: Map out a route for that army to travel to the city of Rabbah, where the Ammonite people live, and map out another route for it to travel to Judah, to the city of Jerusalem, which possesses fortified walls. \
21.21: The king of Babylon will stop and stand at attention at the place where the road divides, where the two roads begin. There, he will ask the gods to provide him with insight as to which way he should go. He will shake marked arrows and see which one falls out; he will ask his household idols what to do; and he will examine the liver of an animal that he has killed for messages from the gods.
21.22: He will receive insight that suggests he should go to Jerusalem and attack the city. It tells him to assemble battering rams to knock down its outer gates. It tells him to give the order to kill the people. It tells his soldiers to shout the battle cry. It tells them to array the battering rams against the city gates, and to construct a siege ramp that allows soldiers to climb over the outer walls. It tells them to build siege walls around the city.
21.23: The peoples of Jerusalem will think that the insight he receives from his gods means nothing. After all, they had sworn oaths of loyalty to him. But the king of Babylon will remind them of the violations of their oath that they have committed, and his soldiers will capture them. \
21.24: So then, tell the people of Israel that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘The king of Babylon has reminded everyone how guilty you are. You have openly rebelled, and everything that you do shows how sinfully you have lived. Since he has reminded everyone of this, your enemies will forcibly capture you.’ \
21.25: As for you, you evil and ungodly ruler of Israel — the moment has arrived during which I, Yahweh, will finally punish your sinful behavior!
21.26: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Take off your royal turban! Remove your crown! Things must change! Consider the important unimportant, and the unimportant important.
21.27: I will utterly destroy the city of Jerusalem! Jerusalem will remain in ruins until the one comes who has the right to rule it; then I will deliver the city over to him.’ \
21.28: As for you, human, declare my messages and tell the Israelite people that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say about the people of Ammon and about how they mocked my people. Tell them, ‘Soldiers have drawn their swords to slaughter the Ammonite people; they have polished their swords in order to destroy people, so that they brightly flash back and forth as they kill with them.
21.29: Although your priests and prophets saw deceitful visions about you and gave you false insight from the gods, those swords will kill you just like any evil and ungodly person. The moment has arrived when Yahweh will finally punish your sinful behavior! \
21.30: Soldiers, put your swords back into their sheaths! I will judge you in the very place where I created you, in the land from whence you came.
21.31: I will show you how indignant I am with you. I am so extremely angry that I will punish you, and I will deliver you to bloodthirsty, brutal men who are experts at destroying people. \
21.32: Fire will destroy you like kindling, and you will die violently there in your own land. No one will ever remember you again. After all, I, Yahweh, have said this will happen!’” \

22.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
22.2: “As for you, human — you must pronounce my legal verdict against the people of Jerusalem. In that city, people murder and oppress other people! Inform the peoples of the city about all the despicable and indecent things that they have done.
22.3: You must tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, ‘You peoples of Jerusalem make other people who live in the city bleed by oppressing and murdering them! By doing that, you ensured that now is the proper moment for me to punish you. You have crafted idols for yourselves that harm you. By doing that, you have made yourselves unfit to worship me! \
22.4: When you oppressed and murdered people, you made yourselves guilty. When you crafted your idols, you became unfit to worship me. Because of your actions, the moment when I will punish you will happen very soon. You will die soon! 22.17: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
22.18: “Human, I consider the Israelite people to be like slag. All of them are like the bronze, tin, iron, and lead that people throw into a furnace in order to purify silver. They have become like the slag that remains after metalworkers purify silver.
22.19: So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘All of you are like slag. So, pay attention to what I am about to do! I am going to gather all of you together inside Jerusalem. \

22.29: Everyone else in Israel extorts one another and robs them. They violently harm people who are poor and destitute, and they unjustly treat the foreigners who live among them. \
22.30: I searched among all the Israelite people for someone who would defend the land and plead with me on its behalf, as if they were repairing a broken wall. If I found that person, I would not destroy the territories of Israel. However, I did not find anyone like that.
22.31: So I have vented my indignant anger against them. Because I was furiously mad, I have destroyed them. I have made them suffer the consequences that their behavior deserves. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’” \

23.35: So this is what the Lord Yahweh says, ‘You have forgotten about me and completely rejected me! As a result, you yourself must suffer the consequences that your obscene and promiscuous behavior deserves.’” \
23.36: Yahweh gave me another message. He said, “Human, you must pronounce my verdict against Oholah and Oholibah. Tell them about the disgusting and illicit things that they have done.

They have even sacrificed the children that they bore for me by burning them alive and offering them to their idols as food. \
23.38: They have even done this to me: On that same day, they desecrated my temple, and they dishonored my Sabbath days.
23.39: On the very same day that they butchered their children as sacrifices to their idols, they entered into my temple so that they could dishonor it! Moreover —pay attention!— they did this right inside my temple. \
23.40: They even dispatched messengers to invite people who lived far away — and, look!— they came! For them, you bathed yourself, applied your makeup, and put on your jewelry.

23.47: That mob will publicly execute them by throwing stones at them and slashing them with their swords. They will kill their children and burn down their houses. \

23.49: You, people of Israel, will suffer the consequences of your obscene behavior; you will accept the punishment for the sins that you committed by worshiping idols. At that time, you will know exactly who I am and what I am like —I am the Lord Yahweh!’” \

24.1: In the ninth year after the Babylonians took us, the people of Israel, away to Babylonia, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
24.2: “Human, write down today’s date, the exact date. Do this because, on this very day, the king of Babylon has besieged the city of Jerusalem with his army. \
24.3: Quote a proverb to these rebellious people. You must tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “Put a cooking pot on the fire; do it! Pour water into it also.
24.4: Put pieces of meat into the pot, all the best pieces — the thigh and the shoulder. Fill up the pot with the best bones!
24.5: Take the best sheep from the flock, and pile logs under the pot for fuel. Boil the meat thoroughly, until you have simmered the bones in the pot as well.” \
24.6: So then, this is what the Lord Yahweh says: “How terrible it will be for Jerusalem, the city where people murder one another! That city is like the proverbial pot, whose rust stays inside it and never comes off. Take the pieces of meat out of the pot one piece at a time; do not throw lots to decide which pieces to take out. \
24.7: Do this because the blood of the people whom the people of Jerusalem murdered, remains inside the city. They spilled that blood on bare rock; they did not even show respect for it by pouring it out on the ground and covering it over with dirt.
24.8: I will spill her own blood on the bare rock, where no one will cover it up in respect. I will do this so that I can rouse my anger and redress the people of Jerusalem.” \
24.9: So this is what the Lord Yahweh says: “How terrible it will be for Jerusalem, that city in which people murder one another! I myself will increase my punishment against it, as though I were piling the firewood high under that pot.
24.10: Pile on more wood and light the fire! Cook the meat until it is done; Stir in the appropriate mixture of spices, and char the bones for the stock. \
24.11: Then set the empty pot on the coals. Do this so that it becomes very hot and its bronze glows, Let the fire melt away everything that is dirty inside it and destroy all its rust.
24.12: That city, the rusty pot, has become worn from so many efforts to clean it, yet its thick rust still will not come off. Consign it to the fire! \
24.13: peoples of Jerusalem, the dirty rust in that pot represents the obscene things that you have done. I have tried to purify you by ceasing such behavior among you, but you refused to stop. As a result, I will purify you only once I have finished punishing you in my anger. \
24.14: I, Yahweh, have spoken. These things will happen soon, and I will certainly do what I have said. I will not hold back; I will not pity you, nor will I choose to do something else. I will hold you accountable for the way you have lived and for the things that you have done.’ That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.” \
24.15: Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
24.16: Human, pay attention to what I am about to do. I am about to take your wife away from you — she who brings you such delight. She will die because of an infectious disease. However, you must not mourn for her or weep, and you must not show your sorrow.
24.17: Moan in your grief, but do so quietly. Do not wail out loudly for your wife. Instead, keep your funerary headdress wrapped on your head and your sandals strapped on your feet, and do not cover the lower part of your face, as grieving people do. Do not eat the food that friends bring to those who are mourning.” \
24.18: Then, one morning I spoke to the people, and that evening my wife died. The next morning, I did what Yahweh told me to do. \
24.19: Then the people said to me, “Tell us what these things mean for us, the things that you are doing.”
24.20: So I said to them, “Yahweh gave me this message.
24.21: He told me to tell you, the people of Israel, ‘This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, “Pay attention to what I am about to do! You are so confidently proud of my temple in Jerusalem; it brings you delight to look at, and you cherish it deeply. Regardless, I am about to allow enemies to destroy and defile it. While that happens, your children, whom you left behind in Jerusalem, will die in the conflict. \
24.22: Then you will do exactly what Ezekiel has just done: you will not cover the lower part of your faces, as grieving people do, nor will you eat the food that friends bring to those who are mourning.
24.23: You will keep your funerary headdresses wrapped on your heads and your sandals strapped on your feet. You will not wail loudly in your grief or weep. Instead, you will waste away because I am punishing you for the wrongs that you have committed. As a result, each one of you will groan to one another in your grief.
24.24: Ezekiel will serve as an object lesson to you. You will do everything that you have seen him do. When all this happens, then you will finally understand who I am and what I am like —I am the Lord Yahweh!”’ \
24.25: Yahweh also said to me, ‘As for you, human, I will soon take my temple away from these people — the building that made them feel safe and strong, the beautiful building that made them rejoice, in which they delighted to look at and longed for. I will take it away along with their own children. When that happens, someone will escape from Jerusalem and will come to you in Babylonia and tell you what has happened there.
24.26: Yahweh also said to me, ‘As for you, human, I will soon take my temple away from these people — the building that made them feel safe and strong, the beautiful building that made them rejoice, in which they delighted to look at and longed for. I will take it away along with their own children. When that happens, someone will escape from Jerusalem and will come to you in Babylonia and tell you what has happened there.
24.27: When this all happens, I will enable you to speak once again. You will converse with the person who has escaped from Jerusalem, and you will no longer remain silent. In this way, you will serve as an object lesson to your people, and then they will finally understand who I am and what I am like —I am Yahweh!” \

25.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
25.2: “Human, turn toward the land where the people of Ammon live and prophesy against them. \
25.3: Tell them that they must listen to my message. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You shouted in triumph when the Babylonians defiled my temple, when they ruined the land of Israel, and when they took the people of Judah away to Babylonia.
25.4: So I am about to let the peoples who live in the desert east of you conquer you. They will set up their tents in your territory and live in your land. They will eat the fruit that grows in your land, and they will drink the milk from your herds.
25.5: I will turn your capital city, Rabbah, into a pasture for camels, and I will turn the rest of the land of Ammon into a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’ \
25.6: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You clapped your hands and stamped your feet to celebrate, and you gloated because you utterly despised the land of Israel and everyone who lived there.
25.7: So I am about to use my power to punish you. I will let other people groups carry you off as plunder. I will destroy you completely, so that you no longer exist as a people in any land. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’ \
25.8: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘The people of Moab and the people of Seir said that the people of Judah were no different from all the other people groups.
25.9: So I am about to leave Moab’s frontier defenseless. The cities that guard its border, the finest cities in that land: Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim,
25.10: I will give to the peoples who live in the desert to the east. They will possess it along with the land of the people of Ammon. I will do this so that the people groups will no longer remember that the people of Ammon ever existed.
25.11: I will also punish the people of Moab. Then they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’ \
25.12: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘The people of Edom hurt the people of Judah because of what Judah did in the past. Because they hurt them so cruelly for what they did, the people of Edom sinned greatly.’
25.13: So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I will use my power to punish the people of Edom. I will destroy both the people and the animals that live there. I will ruin their land completely, from Teman all the way to Dedan, and their enemies will kill them with swords. \
25.14: I will use my people Israel to punish the people of Edom. My people will treat Edom in a way that shows how extremely angry I am. Then the people of Edom will know that I am the one punishing them.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say. \
25.15: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘The Philistines attacked the people of Judah because of what Judah did in the past. Because they utterly despised my people, they tried to destroy them completely because of what Judah did in the past, for they had hated my people for a very long time.’
25.16: So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Because they did that I am about to use my power to punish the Philistines. I will destroy the Cherethites, and I will kill everyone who still lives along the seacoast.
25.17: I will punish them again and again because I am very angry about what they did in the past. When I punish them for what they did, they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’” \

26.1: In the eleventh year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the first day of the month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
26.2: “Human, the people of Tyre gloated over the city of Jerusalem. They said, ‘Aha! Jerusalem was the city that controlled the trade of all the peoples, but now enemies have destroyed her! The trade that used to pass through her has turned toward us instead. Now that Jerusalem lies in ruins, we will grow rich!’ \
26.3: Therefore this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen, Tyre! I am now your enemy. I will cause many people groups to attack you continuously, one after another.
26.4: Their armies will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers. I will scrape away even the soil of that city until nothing remains there but bare rock. \
26.5: The sea will surround the place where the city was and become a place where fishermen do nothing but spread out their nets to dry. I myself have said this. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. The soldiers of those people groups will carry off everything valuable that she owns.
26.6: Enemy soldiers will attack the villages on the mainland that depend on Tyre, and they will kill the people who live there in battle. Then the people of Tyre will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’ \
26.7: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I am about to bring King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon to attack Tyre. He is the greatest king of all, and he will march against you from the north with horses, chariots, horsemen, and a huge army of soldiers.
26.8: He will kill the people who live in your villages on the mainland. He will build a wall of earth all around your city to shut everyone inside, he will pile up a ramp of earth against your city wall so that his soldiers can climb up it, and he will set up large shields to protect his soldiers as they attack. \
26.9: He will bring up heavy beams and pound them against your walls to smash them, and he will tear down your towers with iron tools.
26.10: He will have so many horses that when they charge in, the dust that their hooves stir up will settle over your whole city. Your walls will shake from the thundering noise of his horsemen and his wagons and his chariots when he rides in through your gates after his soldiers have broken through your walls.
26.11: His horses will trample every one of your streets with their hooves. His soldiers will kill your people with their swords, and the sacred stone pillars that you were so proud of will crash to the ground. \
26.12: His soldiers will carry off your wealth and the goods that your merchants sell. They will break down your walls and demolish the beautiful houses that you love. Then they will throw your stones and your timbers and your rubble into the sea.
26.13: I will put an end to the noise of your singing, and no one will hear anyone playing your harps ever again.
26.14: I will make you nothing but bare rock, a place where fishermen spread out their nets. No one will ever rebuild you, because I, Yahweh, have spoken.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
26.15: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say to Tyre, ‘When you fall, the people who live along the coasts will certainly tremble, because they will hear your dying people groaning and your enemies slaughtering people all through your city.
26.16: Then all the rulers of the nations along the sea will step down from their thrones. They will take off their royal robes and strip off their embroidered clothes to show that they are mourning. Instead they will tremble with fear. They will sit on the ground, shuddering over and over, and they will shake with horror at what has happened to you. \
26.17: Then they will sing a funeral song about you. They will sing, “How completely you have perished, you city where seafarers lived! Everyone praised you, and you were powerful out on the sea, you and the people who lived in you. You terrified everyone who lived along the coast!
26.18: Now, on the day when you fall, the people along the coasts tremble; the people on the islands in the sea shake with terror because you are gone.”’ \
26.19: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I will make your city a ruin, like the cities where no one lives anymore. I will overwhelm you completely with disaster, as though the deep sea had risen up and its vast waters had covered you.
26.20: Then I will send you down to join the people who died long ago and went down into the grave. I will make you stay in the world far below the earth, among places that have lain in ruins since ancient times, together with everyone else who has gone down into the grave. You will never again have a place among living people. However, I will give glory to the land where living people dwell.
26.21: I will bring you to a horrifying end, and you will exist no longer. People will search for you, but they will never find you again.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.” \

27.1: Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
27.2: “As for you, human, sing a funeral song about the city of Tyre.
27.3: Say this to Tyre, the city that is where ships come in from the sea, the city full of people that trade with peoples who live along many coasts. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘People of Tyre, you yourself boasted that you were perfectly beautiful. \
27.4: Your territory lies out in the middle of the sea; the ones who built you made you completely beautiful.
27.5: You were like a magnificent ship. Your builders made all your planks out of cypress trees from Senir; they took a cedar tree from Lebanon to make your mast. \
27.6: They made your oars out of oak trees from Bashan; they made your deck out of pine wood from the coasts of Kittim, and they set ivory into it.
27.7: They made your sail out of fine embroidered linen from Egypt, so that people far away could tell that it was you; they made your awning out of blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah. \
27.8: Men from Sidon and Arvad rowed you; your own skilled men, Tyre, were on board, and they sailed you.
27.9: The elders of Gebal and that city’s skilled workers were on board to seal up your leaking seams. Sailors from every ship that sailed the sea came to you to trade for your goods. \
27.10: Men from Persia, Lud, and Put served as soldiers in your army. They hung their shields, helmets, and all their other armor inside your city; they are the ones who made you look magnificent.
27.11: Men from Arvad and your own soldiers stood guard on your walls all around, and men from Gammad guarded your towers. They hung their shields all around on your walls; they are the ones who made you completely beautiful. \
27.12: Merchants from Tarshish traded with you because you had such an enormous amount of goods. They gave you silver, iron, tin, and lead in exchange for your wares.
27.13: Merchants from Javan, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you. They gave you slaves and bronze objects in exchange for your goods. \
27.14: Men from Beth Togarmah gave you workhorses, warhorses, and mules in exchange for your wares.
27.15: Men from Dedan traded with you, and you controlled the trade of the people who lived along many coasts. Those people brought you ivory tusks and ebony, a valuable black wood, as payment. \
27.16: Merchants from Aram traded with you because you produced so many things. They gave you emeralds, purple cloth, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral, and rubies in exchange for your wares.
27.17: Men from Judah and from the land of Israel traded with you. They gave you wheat from Minnith, a food called pannag, honey, olive oil, and balm in exchange for your goods.
27.18: Merchants from Damascus traded with you because you produced so many things and had such great wealth. They brought you wine from Helbon and white wool. \
27.19: Men from Vedan and from Javan near Uzal also traded with you. They brought wrought iron and the spices cassia and sweet cane.
27.20: Merchants from Dedan traded with you. They brought saddle blankets that people put on horses before riding them.
27.21: Merchants from Arabia and all the rulers of Kedar traded with you. They gave you lambs and rams and male goats in exchange for your goods. \
27.22: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah traded with you. They gave you the finest of all the spices, all kinds of precious stones, and gold in exchange for your wares.
27.23: Merchants from Haran, Kanneh, Eden, Sheba, Assyria, and Kilmad also traded with you. \
27.24: In your marketplace those merchants sold you fine clothing, cloaks of blue cloth and embroidered cloth, and multicolored rugs that they had rolled up and tied tightly with cords.
27.25: Ships from Tarshish carried your goods from place to place. People loaded you full of cargo, and you rode very low in the water far out in the middle of the sea. \
27.26: Your rowers took you out into deep water, but a wind from the east will break you apart far out in the middle of the sea.
27.27: On the day when you sink, all of these will go down into the middle of the sea: your wealth, your wares, and your merchandise, your sailors and your pilots and the men who repair your leaking seams, the merchants who trade your goods, all your soldiers who are on board, and the whole crowd of people who are in you. \
27.28: When your pilots cry out, the people who live along the shore will tremble with fear.
27.29: All the men who row will come down from their ships; the sailors and all the pilots who sail the sea will stand on the shore.
27.30: They will cry out loudly about you and weep bitterly; they will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes to show how deeply they grieve. \
27.31: They will shave their heads completely bald and put on rough sackcloth, to show that they are mourning for you; they will weep for you because they feel terrible sorrow, and they will grieve for you very deeply.
27.32: As they wail, they will sing a funeral song for you. They will sing, “No city was ever like Tyre; now she has perished, and she lies silent in the middle of the sea.”
27.33: When your goods went out across the seas, you gave many peoples everything that they wanted. With your great wealth and all your merchandise you made kings all over the earth rich. \
27.34: Now you will break apart far out at sea and sink into deep water; all your merchandise and the whole crowd of people in you will go down with you.
27.35: All the people who live along the coasts shake with horror at what has happened to you; their kings shudder violently, and their faces show how terrified they are.
27.36: Merchants among the nations hiss at you to show their scorn and horror. What has happened to you will horrify people everywhere, and you will never exist again.’” \

28.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
28.2: “Human, say to the ruler of the city of Tyre that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You have become very proud, and you have boasted that you are a god and that you sit on a god’s throne out in the middle of the sea. Yet you are only a human being; you are not a god, even though you think that you are as wise as a god.
28.3: You think that you are wiser than Daniel was and that no one can keep any secret hidden from you. \
28.4: Because you are so wise and understand so much, you have made yourself wealthy; you have acquired gold and silver and stored them in your treasuries.
28.5: You have traded very skillfully because you are so wise, and so you have become even wealthier. Now, because you are so wealthy, you have become very proud.’ \
28.6: Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Because you think that you are as wise as the gods,
28.7: I am about to bring foreigners to attack you, soldiers from the nations that are the most ruthless of all. They will destroy the beautiful things that you created by being so wise with their swords, and they will make everything that made you look magnificent ugly. \
28.8: They will bring you down to the grave. You will die violently, the way soldiers die in battle, there in your city out in the middle of the sea.
28.9: When the men who are about to kill you come to you, you will certainly not claim that you are a god. You are only a human being, not a god, and the men who stab you will have you completely in their power.
28.10: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die a shameful death like people who do not belong to God. This will surely happen because I myself have said it.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.” \
28.11: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
28.12: “Human, sing a funeral song about the king of the city of Tyre. Say to him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You were perfect in every way. You were completely wise and perfectly handsome.
28.13: It was as though you lived in Eden, the garden of God. You wore precious stones of every kind: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, emerald, and garnet. Craftsmen mounted those stones in settings of gold. I prepared all of them for you on the day when I created you. \
28.14: I anointed you and appointed you as a winged creature who guards. I placed you on my own holy mountain, and you walked about there among the glowing stones.
28.15: Everything that you did was perfect from the day when I created you, until you began to do wicked things. \
28.16: Because you traded on such a huge scale, your merchants acted violently everywhere in your city, and you sinned. So I treated you as something unclean and drove you away from my mountain. You winged creature who guards, I destroyed you and removed you from among the glowing stones.
28.17: You became very proud because you were so handsome. Because you loved your own splendor, you ruined the wisdom that you had. So I brought you down and disgraced you completely; I put you on display in front of other kings, and they all stared at you. \
28.18: Because you sinned so many times and traded so dishonestly, you made your own temples unholy. So I caused a fire to break out inside your city, and it burned you up completely. I reduced you to ashes lying on the ground, and everyone who was watching saw it happen.
28.19: All the peoples who knew you shake with horror at what has happened to you. You have come to a terrifying end, and you will never exist again.’” \
28.20: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
28.21: “Human, turn toward the city of Sidon and prophesy against it.
28.22: Say that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You people of Sidon, I am your enemy! By what I do among you I will show how glorious I am. When I punish you and show that I am holy, then people will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. \
28.23: I will send a deadly disease among you, and enemy soldiers will kill people in your streets. They will attack you from every direction, and they will kill your people inside your city. Then people will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.
28.24: The nations all around the people of Israel despise them, but those nations will no longer hurt them or cause them pain. Then the people of Israel will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.’ \
28.25: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I will gather the people of Israel from the peoples among whom I scattered them, and by what I do for them I will show the nations that I am holy. After that, they will live in their own land, the soil that I gave to my servant Jacob.
28.26: They will live there safely. They will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live safely when I punish all the nations around them that despise them. Then they will know that I, Yahweh their God, am the all-powerful God.’” \

29.1: In the tenth year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
29.2: “Human, turn toward Pharaoh, the king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against everyone who lives in the land of Egypt.
29.3: Tell him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen, Pharaoh, king of Egypt! I am now your enemy. You think that you are powerful and safe, like a huge monster that lies among the channels of the Nile River. You boast that the Nile River belongs to you and that you made it for your own benefit. \
29.4: So I will capture you. It will be as though I put hooks in your jaws and made all the fish in your channels stick fast to your scales, and then dragged you up out of the middle of your channels with all those fish still clinging to you.
29.5: I will throw you out into the desert, you and all your people who are like the fish from your channels. You will fall on the open ground, and no one will pick up your body or bury it. I will give your body to the wild animals and the birds for them to eat. \
29.6: Then everyone who lives in Egypt will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. I will punish you because you Egyptians failed the people of Israel when they relied on you to support them.
29.7: When the Israelites asked you for help, you failed them, and you wounded them badly. When they depended on you to hold them up, you could not, and you left them too weak to stand.’ \
29.8: Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I am about to bring an army to attack you with swords, and those soldiers will kill both your people and your animals.
29.9: The land of Egypt will become completely deserted and ruined. Then the people of Egypt will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. I will do this because you, their king, boasted that the Nile River belongs to you because you made it.
29.10: Therefore, listen! I am against you and against the channels of your river. I will ruin the land of Egypt completely and leave it deserted, from Migdol in the north to Syene in the south, as far as the border of the land of Cush. \
29.11: No person will walk through that land, and no animal will walk through it. No one will live there for forty years.
29.12: For forty years I will keep the land of Egypt and all its cities as desolate as the other lands and cities that enemies have devastated. I will scatter the people of Egypt among the other nations and force them to live in foreign lands.’ \
29.13: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘After 40 years have passed, I will gather the people of Egypt back from the nations where I scattered them.
29.14: I will cause them to prosper again. I will bring them back to the region of Pathros in southern Egypt, the land that their ancestors came from. There they will be a weak and unimportant kingdom. \
29.15: Egypt will be the least important kingdom of all, and it will never again make itself greater than the other nations. I will make its people so few that they will never again rule over other nations.
29.16: The people of Israel will never again trust the Egyptians to help them. Instead, whenever the Israelites remember how they sought help from Egypt, they will remember that they sinned by doing that. Then they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh, the all-powerful God.’” \
29.17: In the twenty-seventh year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the first day of the first month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
29.18: “Human, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon made his army work extremely hard when they attacked the city of Tyre. The soldiers carried such heavy loads that they rubbed all the hair off their heads and rubbed the skin off their shoulders. Yet neither Nebuchadnezzar nor his army received anything from Tyre to pay them for all the hard work that they did there. \
29.19: Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I am about to give the land of Egypt to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. He will carry away all the wealth of Egypt and take everything valuable in that land as plunder. That wealth will be the pay for his army.
29.20: I have given him the land of Egypt as the pay for the hard work that his army did when they attacked Tyre, because they did that work for me.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
29.21: On that day I will cause the people of Israel to become strong again, and I will enable you, Ezekiel, to speak freely among them. Then they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.” \

30.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
30.2: “Human, prophesy and say that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Wail and cry out loudly, because a terrible day is coming!
30.3: That day is near; the day when I, Yahweh, will punish people is very close. It will be a time of gloom and disaster, a time when I judge the nations. \
30.4: An enemy army will come to attack Egypt with swords, and the people of Cush will suffer terribly. When those soldiers kill many people in Egypt, they will carry away the crowds of Egyptians as captives, and they will tear down everything that holds the nation together.
30.5: The soldiers of Cush, Put, and Lud, all the foreign troops who fight for Egypt, the people of Cub, and the Judeans who live in Egypt will all die in battle along with the Egyptians.’ \
30.6: I, Yahweh, say this, ‘The nations that help Egypt will fall, and the Egyptians will no longer be able to boast about how strong they are. Enemy soldiers will kill them in battle everywhere in Egypt, from Migdol in the north to Syene in the south.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
30.7: ‘I will make the land of Egypt as desolate as the other lands that I have devastated, and its cities will lie in ruins like the other cities that enemies have destroyed. \
30.8: Then the people of Egypt will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God, because I will set fire to Egypt and defeat every nation that helps her.
30.9: On that day I will send messengers out from me in ships to terrify the people of Cush, who until then think that they are safe. They will tremble with fear when I punish Egypt. Be sure of this: that day is coming!’ \
30.10: I, the Lord Yahweh, say this, ‘I will use King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon to put an end to the crowds of people in Egypt.
30.11: I am bringing Nebuchadnezzar and his army, soldiers who are more ruthless than any other people, to ruin the land. They will attack Egypt with their swords, and they will kill so many people that dead bodies will lie all over the land. \
30.12: I will dry up the channels of the Nile River, and I will hand the land over to evil men. I will use foreigners to ruin the land and everything in it.’ I, Yahweh, have spoken. \
30.13: I, the Lord Yahweh, say this, ‘I will completely destroy the worthless idols that people worship in the city of Memphis. No one will ever rule as a prince in the land of Egypt again, and I will terrify everyone who lives in Egypt.
30.14: I will make the region of Pathros in southern Egypt desolate. I will set fire to the city of Zoan, and I will punish the people of the city of Thebes. \
30.15: Because I am extremely angry, I will punish the city named Sin, the fortress that protects Egypt, and I will kill the crowds of people in the city of Thebes.
30.16: I will set fire to Egypt. The people who live in the city named Sin will suffer agonizing pain, enemies will break through the walls of the city of Thebes, and enemies will attack the city of Memphis every day. \
30.17: Enemy soldiers will kill the young men of the cities of Aven and Pi Beseth, and they will take the people of those cities away as captives.
30.18: In the city of Tahpanhes it will be a day of disaster, because there I will put an end to Egypt’s power to dominate other nations, and the Egyptians will no longer be able to boast about how strong they are. The people there will experience constant trouble, and enemies will take away the people of Tahpanhes and the surrounding communities as captives.
30.19: That is how I will punish Egypt, and then people will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God!’” \
30.20: In the eleventh year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the seventh day of the first month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
30.21: “Human, I have destroyed the military power of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. No one has done anything to restore that power, just as no one puts medicine on a broken arm or wraps a bandage around it so that it can heal and grow strong enough to grip a sword again. Egypt will never recover its strength for war. \
30.22: Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I am now the enemy of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. I will take away all the power that he still has, as though I broke both of his arms, the arm that is still strong and the arm that I have already broken, and I will make the sword drop out of his hand so that he can fight no longer.
30.23: I will scatter the people of Egypt so that they live among many other nations, far away in foreign lands.
30.24: I will make the king of Babylon strong, and I will use him to carry out my judgment. I will shatter the power of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh will groan loudly in front of the king of Babylon, the way a man groans when someone has wounded him so badly that he is about to die. \
30.25: I will make the king of Babylon strong, but Pharaoh will become completely helpless. Then people will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God, because I will make the king of Babylon the one who carries out my judgment, and he will attack the land of Egypt.
30.26: I will scatter the people of Egypt so that they live among many other nations, far away in foreign lands. Then they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God!’” \

31.1: In the eleventh year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the first day of the third month, Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
31.2: “Human, say to Pharaoh the king of Egypt and to the crowds of people he rules, ‘You think that no one has ever been as great as you are. \
31.3: Consider Assyria. That nation was once like a cedar tree in Lebanon, a tree with beautiful branches that gave shade to everything under it. It grew very tall, and its top rose above the thick foliage around it.
31.4: Plenty of water made that tree grow big, and deep underground springs made it grow tall. Those springs sent their streams flowing all around the ground where the tree grew, and they sent channels of water out to every other tree in the field. \
31.5: So that tree grew taller than all the other trees in the field. It put out many limbs, and its branches grew long and spread out, because it had so much water.
31.6: Birds of every kind built their nests in its limbs, and wild animals of every kind gave birth to their young under its branches. The people of many great nations used to live in its shade, safe under its protection.
31.7: That tree was magnificent, because it was so big and its branches were so long. Its roots reached down to plenty of water. \
31.8: Not even the cedar trees in God’s garden could match it. No cypress tree had limbs like its limbs, and no plane tree had branches like its branches. No tree in God’s garden was as beautiful as that one.
31.9: I made it beautiful, giving it many branches, and the rulers of all the other nations, who were like the other trees in Eden, the garden of God, envied it. \
31.10: So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, “That tree grew very tall and pushed its top up above the thick foliage, and it became arrogant because it was so tall.
31.11: Therefore I handed it over to a ruler who was mightier than all the other nations, and he certainly did to it what it deserved. I drove that nation out because it had acted so wickedly. \
31.12: Foreigners, soldiers more ruthless than any other people, chopped that tree down and left it lying there. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys, and those soldiers broke its boughs to pieces in every ravine in the land. All the peoples who had lived in its shade went away and abandoned it. \
31.13: Birds of every kind came and settled on the trunk of that fallen tree, and wild animals of every kind stayed among its broken branches.
31.14: I did all this so that no other nation that flourishes like a well-watered tree would ever grow so tall again, or push its top up above the thick foliage, and so that not even the mightiest of those trees, none of the ones that drink plenty of water, would ever stand so high again. I have appointed them all to die and to go down to the world below the earth, along with human beings who go down into the grave.” \
31.15: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, “On the day when that tree went down to the place where dead people go, I caused people to mourn for it. I covered over the deep springs that watered it and held back their rivers, so that the abundant water stopped flowing. Because that tree fell, I made the whole land of Lebanon mourn, and I caused all the other trees of the field to wither. \
31.16: When the nations heard that it had fallen, I made them tremble with fear, for I brought that tree down to the place where dead people go, together with all those who go down into the grave. Down in the world below the earth, the other trees of Eden, the choicest and finest trees of Lebanon, all the ones that had plenty of water, found comfort when it came down to join them. \
31.17: Those other nations also went down with it to the place where dead people go, to join those whom enemies had killed with swords. They had been its strength; they were its allies, and they had lived under its protection among the nations.
31.18: You Egyptians think that no tree in Eden was ever as glorious and as great as you are. However, I will bring you down, along with those trees of Eden, to the world below the earth. You will lie there dead, among men who do not have the mark of circumcision on their bodies, together with those whom enemies have killed with swords. This whole parable about the great tree Assyria describes what I have decreed for Pharaoh and all the crowds of people he rules.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.’” \

32.1: In the twelfth year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the first day of the twelfth month, Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
32.2: “Human, sing a funeral song about Pharaoh the king of Egypt. Say this to him, ‘You think that you are like a young lion that hunts among the nations, but really you are like a monster that lives in the sea. You thrash about in the streams of your river, churning up the water with your feet and making those streams muddy. \
32.3: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, “I will gather the armies of many peoples, and I will spread my net over you, and those armies will haul you up in my dragnet.
32.4: Then I will fling you down on the ground and toss you out in an open field. I will let every kind of bird come and settle on you, and I will let wild animals from everywhere eat your dead body until they are full. \
32.5: I will spread your flesh over the mountains, and I will fill the valleys with your rotting remains.
32.6: Your blood will soak the ground all the way to the mountains, and it will fill the ravines. \
32.7: When I put an end to you, I will cover the sky and darken the stars in it. I will hide the sun behind a cloud, and the moon will not shine.
32.8: I will darken every shining light in the sky above you, and I will bring darkness and disaster on your land.” That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
32.9: “I will deeply disturb many peoples when I cause enemies to take you and your people to different nations, even to lands that you have never been to.
32.10: I will horrify many peoples because of what happens to you. Their kings will shudder violently because they will be afraid that I will do the same to them. On the day when you fall, they will tremble constantly, each one fearing for his own life.” \
32.11: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, “The army of the king of Babylon will come to attack you.
32.12: I will let mighty warriors, the most ruthless soldiers of all the nations, kill your huge crowds of people with their swords. Those warriors will ruin everything that the people of Egypt boast about, and they will destroy all the crowds of people there. \
32.13: I will also destroy all the cattle that graze beside Egypt’s abundant waters. Never again will any person or any animal walk in those waters and stir up the mud.
32.14: Then I will let the waters of Egypt settle, and I will let its rivers flow smoothly and quietly.” That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
32.15: “The people of Egypt will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God because I will turn the land of Egypt into an empty wasteland and strip the land of everything that fills it, and I will strike down everyone who lives there.
32.16: This is a funeral song, and the women of the nations will chant it. They will chant it as they mourn for Egypt and for all its crowds of people.” That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’” \
32.17: In the twelfth year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month, Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
32.18: “Human, cry loudly for the crowds of people in Egypt. Command Egypt and the people of other mighty nations to go down to the world below the earth, to join those who go down into the grave. \
32.19: Taunt the people of Egypt like this, ‘You are no more delightful than anyone else! Go down and lie down there with godless men!’
32.20: The people of Egypt will fall down dead among all those whom enemies have killed with swords. I have handed Egypt over to enemies who carry swords; those enemies will drag Egypt away, along with all its crowds of people.
32.21: From the place where dead people go, the mightiest of the warriors will speak to Pharaoh and to those who helped him. They will say, ‘They have come down here, and now they lie here, godless men, whom enemies killed with swords.’ \
32.22: Assyria is there, along with its whole army, and the graves of its soldiers lie all around it. Enemies killed every one of them with swords.
