32.23: Their graves lie in the deepest part of the grave, and the graves of Assyria’s army surround its burial place. Enemies killed every one of them with swords, those soldiers who once terrified people while they were still alive. \
32.24: Elam is there, along with all its crowds of people, and their graves surround its burial place. Enemies killed every one of them with swords. They went down to the world below the earth without God, and while they were still alive they terrified people. Now they suffer disgrace along with those who go down into the grave.
32.25: People have made a place for Elam to lie down among all those whom enemies killed, together with all its crowds of people, and their graves surround it. They are all godless, and enemies killed them all with swords, because while they were still alive they terrified people. So now they suffer disgrace along with those who go down into the grave. People have laid Elam among all those whom enemies killed. \
32.26: Meshech and Tubal are there, along with all their crowds of people, and their graves surround them. They are all godless, and enemies stabbed them all to death with swords, because while they were still alive they too terrified people.
32.27: They do not lie among the mighty warriors who fell in battle long ago and went down to the place where dead people go carrying their weapons of war. People laid the swords of those warriors under their heads and put their shields on their bones, because while they were alive those warriors terrified people. \
32.28: As for you, Pharaoh, I will shatter you, and you will lie down dead among godless men, together with those whom enemies killed with swords.
32.29: Edom is there, with its kings and all its leaders. In spite of all their strength, people have laid them among those whom enemies killed with swords. They lie there with godless men, along with those who go down into the grave. \
32.30: All the princes of the north are there, and every Sidonian is there too. They went down with those whom enemies killed. They were strong and terrorized people but now they are ashamed. They lie there without God, together with those whom enemies killed with swords, and they suffer disgrace along with those who go down into the grave. \
32.31: Pharaoh will see all of them, and he will find comfort in knowing that others suffered the same fate as all his crowds of people — Pharaoh and his whole army, whom enemies killed with swords.” That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
32.32: “I allowed Pharaoh to terrify people while they were still alive, so now I will lay him down among godless men, together with those whom enemies killed with swords — Pharaoh and all his crowds of people. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.” \

33.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
33.2: “Human, speak to your fellow Israelites and say this to them, ‘Suppose I send an enemy army to attack a country, and the people of that country choose one of their men and appoint him to be their watchman.
33.3: Suppose he sees the enemy army coming to attack the country, and he blows a ram’s horn to warn the people.
33.4: Then if someone hears the sound of the horn but pays no attention to the warning, and the enemy soldiers come and kill him, he is responsible for his own death. \
33.5: He heard the sound of the horn, but he paid no attention to the warning, so he is responsible for his own death. If he had paid attention to the warning, he would have saved his own life.
33.6: But suppose the watchman sees the enemy army coming and does not blow the horn to warn the people, and the enemy soldiers come and kill one of them. That person will die because of his own sin, but I will hold the watchman responsible for that person’s death.’ \
33.7: Now as for you, human, I have appointed you to be like a watchman for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, and warn them for me.
33.8: Suppose I tell you to tell a sinful person that he is certainly going to die because of his sins, but you do not say anything to warn that sinful person to stop sinning. Then that sinful person will die because he has sinned, but I will hold you responsible for his death, since you did not act to prevent it.
33.9: But suppose you do warn that sinful person to change how he is living, but he does not change how he is living. Then he will die because of his sinful behavior but you will have saved your own life from my punishing. \
33.10: Now you human, tell the people of Israel that they keep saying, ‘We feel great emotional and physical pain because we are guilty because we sinned by rebelling against God. How can we go on living?’
33.11: Say this to them, ‘I, the Lord Yahweh, solemnly declare and swear by my own life, I am certainly not pleased when wicked people die. Instead, I am pleased when they stop behaving wickedly and so go on living. So repent! Stop your evil behavior! You people of Israel, there is no reason at all for you to die!’ \
33.12: Now you human, say this to your fellow Israelites, ‘If righteous people start to sin, I will not consider the righteous things they did before when I punish them. And if wicked people stop behaving wickedly, I will not punish them for the sins that they committed before. Righteous people who start to sin will not go on living just because they were righteous before.
33.13: Suppose I tell a righteous person that he will certainly go on living, but then he relies on the righteous things he has done and starts doing what is wrong. I will not remember any of the righteous things that he did. He will die because of the wrong things that he is doing. \
33.14: But suppose I tell a wicked person that he will certainly die, but then he stops sinning and starts doing what is just and right.
33.15: Suppose he gives back what someone handed him to guarantee a loan, and he returns what he stole, and he obeys my rules that cause people to flourish, so that he no longer does what is wrong. Then he will certainly go on living; he will not die.
33.16: I will forgive any of the sins that he committed. He has done what is just and right, so he will certainly go on living. \
33.17: Yet your fellow Israelites say that I, the Lord, do not act fairly. But it is what they do that is not fair.
33.18: If a righteous person stops doing what is right and starts doing what is wrong, he will die because of those wrong things.
33.19: But if a wicked person stops behaving wickedly and starts doing what is just and right, he will go on living because of those good things.
33.20: But you people still say that I, the Lord, do not act fairly. I will judge each one of you people of Israel according to how you have behaved.’” \
33.21: In the twelfth year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a man who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, “Our enemies have captured the city!”
33.22: The evening before that man arrived, the power of Yahweh came over me. By the time the man reached me the next morning, Yahweh had enabled me to speak again, so I could no longer keep silent. \
33.23: Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
33.24: “Human, the people who are living among the ruins in the land of Israel keep saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet Yahweh gave him this whole land to possess. We are many, so Yahweh has surely given this land to us to possess.’ \
33.25: So tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You eat meat that still has the animal’s blood in it. You trust your idols and worship them. You murder people. So you will certainly not go on possessing this land!
33.26: You rely on your swords to get what you want. You do detestable things. Each of you has sexual relations with another man’s wife. So you will certainly not go on possessing this land!’ \
33.27: Also tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I swear by my own life, enemy soldiers will kill with their swords those who are living among the ruins. I will let wild animals eat those who are out in the open country. Those who are hiding in fortresses and caves will die from a deadly disease.
33.28: I will make the land completely empty and ruined. The people will no longer be proud of how strong their country is. The mountains of Israel will become so desolate that no one will travel through them.
33.29: Then, when I have made the land empty and ruined because of all the detestable things that they have done, they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God!’ \
33.30: As for you, human, your fellow Israelites are talking about you as they stand beside the walls and in the doorways of their houses, where people gather to talk. They keep saying to one another, ‘Come on, let us go and hear the message that Yahweh is giving!’
33.31: So my people come to you in large crowds, and they sit down in front of you and listen to what you say. But they do not do what you tell them. All they talk about is how they are planning to become richer. \
33.32: Indeed, they think of you as nothing more than an entertainer, someone who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays a musical instrument well. They listen to what you say, but they do not do it.
33.33: When everything that you have prophesied happens, and it certainly will happen, then they will realize that a true prophet was living among them.” \

34.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
34.2: “Human, prophesy against the leaders of Israel, the men who should be caring for my people the way that shepherds care for their sheep. Say to these men who should be like shepherds that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Terrible things will happen to you leaders of Israel, because you have been taking care of only yourselves! You should be like shepherds who take care of their flocks.
34.3: Instead, you use my people to enrich yourselves. It is as though you eat the fat of the sheep and make your clothes from their wool and slaughter the healthiest animals, but you do not take care of the flock at all. \
34.4: It is as though you have not strengthened the weak sheep. You have not healed the sick ones. You have not bandaged the injured ones. You have not brought back the ones that became scattered. You have not searched for the ones that got lost. Instead, you have ruled my people harshly and cruelly.
34.5: So my people scattered, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. Then their enemies attacked them and plundered them, as wild animals devour sheep that have no shepherd. So they scattered more.
34.6: My people wander like sheep over every mountain and on every high hill. They scatter all across the land, and no one at all searches for them. \
34.7: Therefore, you leaders who should be shepherding my people, listen to what I, Yahweh, say:
34.8: I swear by my own life — this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare — that enemies have carried my people away as plunder and destroyed them as wild animals devour sheep because they had no shepherd. You who should have shepherded my people did not search for them. Instead, you fed only yourselves and did not take care of my people. \
34.9: Therefore, you leaders who should be shepherding my people, listen to what I, Yahweh, say:
34.10: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: Listen, I am now the enemy of you leaders! I will demand that you give my people back to me. I will remove you from taking care of them, so that you can no longer feed only yourselves. I will rescue my people from you, and you will never again plunder and destroy them as wild animals devour sheep. \
34.11: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: Watch what I am about to do! I myself will search for my people, and I myself will take care of them.
34.12: Just as a shepherd takes care of his sheep when he is among his sheep that have scattered, so I will take care of my people. I will rescue them from every place where enemies scattered them during that terrible time.
34.13: I will bring my people out from the other peoples and gather them from the other lands, and I will bring them back to their own land. I will care for them like a shepherd on the mountains of Israel, alongside the streams, and in every place in the land where people live. \
34.14: I will take care of them as a shepherd takes care of his sheep by giving them good pastures, and giving them a home on the high mountains of Israel. I will give them a good home in which to rest, and it will be as though they are feeding in rich pastures among the mountains of Israel.
34.15: I myself will take care of my people, and I myself will enable them to rest. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
34.16: I will search for the ones that got lost, and I will bring back the ones that enemies chased away. I will heal the injured ones and strengthen the sick ones. However, I will destroy the fat and strong ones. I will take care of all of them justly. \
34.17: As for you who are like my flock of sheep, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: I am about to judge between each of you who are like sheep, and between each of you who are like rams and male goats.
34.18: You powerful ones are like strong animals that should be satisfied with feeding on the good pasture. Yet it is as though you also trample down the rest of the pasture with your feet! You are like animals that should be satisfied with drinking the clear water; and yet you also churn up mud in the rest of the water with your feet!
34.19: So the rest of my people are like the flock that must feed on the grass that you trampled and drink the water that you muddied. \
34.20: Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say to my people: I myself am the one who is about to judge between those of you who are strong like fat sheep and those of you who are weak like thin sheep.
34.21: I will do this because It is as though you are the powerful sheep who shove the weak sheep aside with your sides and your shoulders and gore all of them with your horns, until you have driven them away from the pasture. \
34.22: I will rescue my people, and no one will ever abuse them again. I will judge between each one of my people.
34.23: I will appoint over them one leader who will care for them the way that a shepherd cares for his flock. He will be a descendant of my servant David. He himself will take care of my people, and he himself will be as their shepherd.
34.24: I, Yahweh, will be their God, and that descendant of my servant David will be the ruler among them. This will surely happen because I, Yahweh, have said this. \
34.25: I will promise my people that they will live peacefully. I will remove every kind of dangerous animal from the land, so that my people can live safely even in the wilderness and sleep safely even in the forests.
34.26: I will bless my people in those areas and in all of the land around my sacred hill. I will send rain at the proper times, and by that rain I will bless them.
34.27: The trees in the fields will produce their fruit, and the ground will produce its crops, and my people will live safely in their land. When I rescue them from the people who have caused them to be slaves, they will know that I, Yahweh, the all-powerful God, have done this for them. \
34.28: The people of other nations will never plunder them again, and wild animals will no longer devour them. They will live safely, and there will be no one to frighten them.
34.29: I will make them famous for how securely I establish them in the land. They will never again need to leave the land because they lack food, and people of other nations will never again humiliate them. \
34.30: Then they will know that I, Yahweh their God, am with them, and that they, the people of Israel, are my people. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
34.31: You are my people, like a flock of sheep that I take care of in my own pasture. You are human beings, and I am your God. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’” \

35.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
35.2: “Human, become an opponent of the people of Edom located at Mount Seir and prophesy against those people.
35.3: Tell them, ‘This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: Listen, you people who live around Mount Seir! I am your enemy! I will punish you by turning your land into an empty wasteland where no one lives. \
35.4: I will turn your cities into heaps of rubble, and as for your land, it will become empty. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.
35.5: I will do that because you have always hated the Israelites, and you delivered them over to soldiers who killed them with swords. You did that when terrible things were happening to them, at the time when I finally punished them for their sins.
35.6: Therefore, I swear by my own life — this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare — that I will deliver you over to people who will kill you, and killers will pursue you. I swear that because you hated the life of your kinsmen, killers will pursue you. \
35.7: I will make the region of Mount Seir a completely desolate area. I will even destroy anyone who travels back and forth through it.
35.8: I will cover your mountains with the corpses of people whom your enemies will kill. Those whom soldiers kill with their swords will lie dead on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your stream beds.
35.9: I will make your land empty forever; no one will ever live in your cities again. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. \
35.10: You said that the two nations, Israel and Judah, and their two lands would belong to you, and that you would take possession of them. You said that even though I, Yahweh, was present there.
35.11: Therefore, I swear by my own life — this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare — that I will treat you as harshly as you treated my people when you were angry at them and envied them because you hated them. The Israelites will know who I am by how I judge you. \
35.12: Then you will also know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. I have heard all of the insulting things that you said about the land of Israel. You said that no one lived there anymore and that you could now take it and everything in it for yourselves.
35.13: You Edomites boasted arrogantly against me and said many things to insult me, and I myself heard all of it. \
35.14: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: I will devastate your land so completely that people all over the world will rejoice.
35.15: They will rejoice as much as you rejoiced when the land that I gave to the Israelites became desolate, because I will do the same thing to you. Mount Seir and all the rest of Edom will become completely empty. Then people will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’” \

36.1: “As for you, human, prophesy about the mountains in the land of Israel. Tell the Israelites to listen to this message from me, Yahweh, about the mountains of Israel!
36.2: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, Israel’s enemies gloated over them and claimed that these age-old mountains now belong to them.’
36.3: Because of that, prophesy and say, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: I say these things because the survivors from various nations all around greatly desired these mountains and they took possession of them. People everywhere gossiped about them and spread malicious reports about them. \
36.4: Therefore, listen to what I, the Lord Yahweh, say about the mountains of Israel. I, the Lord Yahweh, am speaking about the mountains and the hills, the ravines and the valleys, the ruins where no one lives any longer, and the cities that people abandoned, cities that survivors of the surrounding nations plundered and ridiculed.
36.5: Because of these things, I, the Lord Yahweh, say this: I swear that I am fiercely jealous for what is mine and that is why I have declared that I will punish the nations that have survived, and especially all the people of Edom. They joyfully and scornfully seized my land for themselves so that they could plunder its pastures.’
36.6: Therefore prophesy about the land of Israel. Say about the mountains and the hilltops, the ravines and the valleys, that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen to me! I have spoken because I am jealous and very angry, since the other nations have humiliated those who should possess them. \
36.7: Therefore, I, myself, the Lord Yahweh, say this: I take a solemn oath and swear that I will humiliate those very nations that are around the land of Israel. \
36.8: But the mountains of Israel will grow trees that produce plenty of fruit for my people Israel, because my people will soon come home.
36.9: Indeed, watch what I will do for Israel; I will bless the land. Soon people will plow its soil and plant seed in it. \
36.10: I will greatly increase the number of people who live there. They will be all the people of Israel, every one of them. People will live in the cities again, and they will rebuild the broken buildings.
36.11: I will increase the number of people and animals there, and they will all have many offspring. I will cause people to live there as they did long ago, and I will make them more prosperous than they were at the beginning. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.
36.12: I will cause my people Israel to go back and forth on the land. They will possess it, and it will belong to them permanently. Never again will they have to leave there. \
36.13: I, the Lord Yahweh, say this: People are saying about the land of Israel that it destroys those who live there and that it loses its peoples.
36.14: Therefore, from now on, the land will not destroy the people who live there, or cause its peoples to leave there. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
36.15: Never again will I let the people of other nations insult or revile this land, and never again will this land fail the people of Israel. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’” \
36.16: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
36.17: “Human, when the Israelite people were living in their own land, they made it a disgusting place by the way that they lived and by the things that they did. I considered the way that they behaved to be as repulsive as a filthy menstruation rag.
36.18: So I punished them severely, because they had murdered many people in the land and because they had made the land a disgusting place by worshiping idols there. \
36.19: I scattered them among many nations and lands. I punished them for the evil way that they had lived and for the evil things that they had done.
36.20: Yet wherever they went among those nations, they caused people to think badly of me, the one who is holy. The people in those places said about them, ‘These people belong to Yahweh, and yet he was not able to keep them in his land.’
36.21: But I cared that people thought that I was not holy because the Israelite people had caused people to believe that among the nations wherever they went. \
36.22: Therefore, tell the Israelite people that I, the Lord Yahweh, say this, ‘You Israelite people, I will do what I am about to do not because you deserve it. No, I will act in order to show people that I am the holy one, since you caused people to think that I am not powerfully holy among the nations wherever you went.
36.23: I will show that I am the powerful and holy one, rather than the one whom the people of the nations scorn because you caused them to think that no one should respect me. Then, when they see me show that I am powerfully holy by what I do for you, the people of those nations will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
36.24: I will take you out of those nations. I will gather you from all those lands and bring you back to your own land.
36.25: I will remove from you everything that made you unacceptable to me. I will cause you to stop worshiping all of your idols. It will be as though I sprinkled clean water on you and made you completely clean. \
36.26: I will give to you a completely new way of thinking and motivate you in a new way. I will cause you to stop being stubborn, and I will cause you to want to obey me.
36.27: I will put my Spirit within you and I will make it possible for you to live in the way that I have commanded and for you to carefully obey my instructions.
36.28: Then you will live in the land that I gave to your ancestors. You will be my people, and I myself will be your God. \
36.29: I will rescue you from everything that made you unacceptable to me. I will make your grain grow plentifully, and I will never again cause you to lack food.
36.30: I will cause your fruit trees and your fields to produce plenty of food, so that the people of other nations will never again ridicule you because you do not have enough to eat.
36.31: Then you will think about how evil your behavior was and about the wicked things that you did, and you will hate yourselves because you sinned so much by doing those detestable things. \
36.32: I want you to know that I will do these things, but not because you deserve for me to do them. I, the Lord Yahweh, declare this. You Israelite people should feel deep shame and disgrace because of the way that you have behaved!
36.33: I, the Lord Yahweh, say this: At the time when I forgive you all of your sins, I will cause people to live in your cities again, and they will rebuild the ruined places.
36.34: People will farm the land that was empty. It will no longer be desolate for everyone who passes by to see. \
36.35: Then people will say, “This land was empty but now it has become as fertile as the garden of Eden, and the cities that enemies had ruined and torn down and left empty are now strong and full of people!”
36.36: Then the nations that I have allowed to remain around you will know that I, Yahweh, have enabled you to rebuild what enemies had torn down and to plant crops again where the land had been empty. I, Yahweh, have promised this, and I will do it. \
36.37: I, the Lord Yahweh, say this: Once again I will respond when the Israelite people ask me to do this for them: I will make their people as numerous as a flock of sheep.
36.38: They will be like a flock of sheep that belong to Yahweh, like the flock of sheep that fills Jerusalem when people bring them there to sacrifice during the yearly festivals. The cities that are now in ruins will be full like that, but of people. Then they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’” \

37.1: Yahweh took hold of me, and by his Spirit he brought me out from where I was and set me down in the middle of the valley. Now the valley was full of human bones.
37.2: He led me all around among the bones. I saw that there was a huge amount of bones lying on the ground all through the valley, and I saw that the bones were completely dry.
37.3: He asked me, “Human, can these bones become alive again?” I answered, “Lord Yahweh, only you know that.” \
37.4: Then he said to me, “Prophesy to these bones. Say to them, ‘You dry bones, listen to this message from Yahweh!’
37.5: Tell these bones that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say to them, ‘Watch this! I am going to cause breath to enter you, and you will become alive again.
37.6: I will attach tendons to you, and I will cause flesh to grow on you, and I will cover you with skin. I will put breath in you, and you will become alive again. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’” \
37.7: So I prophesied just what Yahweh had commanded me to say. While I was prophesying, I heard a noise, and I realized that it was the rattling of the bones coming together, each bone joining to the bone that belonged next to it!
37.8: As I watched, I saw tendons appear on the bones, and then flesh grew on them, and then skin covered over the surface of them. However, they were not breathing. \
37.9: Then he said to me, “Human, prophesy to the breath. Tell the breath that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Breath, come from every direction and enter into these dead people, so that they may become alive again.’”
37.10: So I prophesied just what he had commanded me to say, and breath entered them. They became alive and stood up on their feet, and became a vast, enormous army. \
37.11: Then he said to me, “Human, these bones represent all the people of Israel. Listen; they keep saying that they have lost all of their strength, that they have nothing left to hope for, and that they have ended as a nation.
37.12: So prophesy and tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen carefully to this, my people: It will be as though I will open your graves and bring you up out of them and make you live again when I bring you back to the land of Israel. \
37.13: When it is as though I am opening your graves and bringing you up out of them, then you my people will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.
37.14: I will put my Spirit in you, and it will be as though you will become alive again, and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the one who has promised this and that I am the one who has done it. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.’” \
37.15: Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
37.16: “Now you human, get a shaft of wood and write on it, ‘This represents Judah and the Israelite tribes that belong with Judah.’ Then get another shaft of wood and write on it, ‘This represents the Israelite tribes associated with Joseph, that is, it is the shaft of the tribe of Ephraim, and all of the Israelite tribes that belong with Ephraim.’
37.17: Then align the two pieces of wood with each other as one piece of wood so that they become like one shaft of wood in your hand. \
37.18: When your fellow Israelites ask you to explain to them what you mean by doing this,
37.19: tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen well! I am going to take the piece of wood that represents Joseph, the part of Israel that the tribe of Ephraim controls, along with the Israelite tribes that belong with Ephraim. I will take them together, and then I will join them to the piece of wood that represents Judah. I will make them to be one piece of wood, and I will hold them as one piece of wood in my hand.’
37.20: As you say this, hold in your hand the pieces of wood on which you wrote, where your fellow Israelites can see them. \
37.21: Then tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen well! I am going to take the Israelite people out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every direction and bring them back to their own land.
37.22: I will make them to be one nation in that land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will rule over all of them. They will not be two nations any more, and they will never again separate into two kingdoms.
37.23: They will no longer make themselves unacceptable to me by worshiping their idols and their disgusting images, or by their many ways of rebelling against me. I will rescue them from all the places where they have been living and sinning, and I will forgive them for sinning. They will be my people, and I myself will be their God. \
37.24: A descendant of my servant David will be their king, and he alone will rule over all of them, taking care of them as a shepherd takes care of his flock. They will live in the way that I have said is right, and they will carefully obey all of my laws.
37.25: They will live in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, the land where their ancestors lived. They and their children and their grandchildren will live there forever, and the one who is the descendant of my servant David will be their ruler forever. \
37.26: I will make an agreement with them that will make a peaceful relationship possible between us; it will be an agreement that lasts forever for them. I will establish them in that land and cause them to become very numerous, and I will put my temple among them forever.
37.27: I will live among them and protect them; I will be their God, and they themselves will be my people.
37.28: When my holy dwelling place is among the Israelite people forever, then the other nations will know that I, Yahweh, the all-powerful God, am the one who makes Israel holy.’” \

38.1: Yahweh gave me another message. He said to me,
38.2: “Human, become an opponent of Gog, who is from the land of Magog and who is the most important ruler over the regions of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
38.3: Tell him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Gog, you who are the most important ruler over Meshech and Tubal, be aware that I am your enemy! \
38.4: I will turn you around and force you to go wherever I want you to go, as though I had put hooks in your jaws. I will bring you out for battle, you and your whole army, your horses and the men who ride them. All of them will be wearing full armor, a huge crowd of men carrying both large shields and small shields. Every one of them is skillful at using his sword.
38.5: Soldiers from Persia, Cush, and Put will go along with your army, and all of them will carry shields and wear helmets.
38.6: The army of Gomer with all of its many soldiers will go with you, and so will the army of Beth Togarmah, which lies in the far north, with all of its groups of soldiers. The armies from many peoples will go with you. \
38.7: Get ready! Prepare yourself well, you and all the troops that you have gathered around you, and be ready to command them.
38.8: A long time from now I will summon you for battle. After many years have passed, you will attack a land where the people have recovered from war. They are the people whom I will have gathered from many peoples and settled again all through the land of Israel, which has been in ruins for a very long time. Those are the very people whom I will have brought out from among the peoples, and all of them will be living there peacefully.
38.9: You must go and fight, advancing as suddenly and violently as a storm. Your troops and the many peoples who come with you will be so many that they will spread like a cloud over the whole land. \
38.10: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say will happen: At that time, you will think about doing something evil, and you will make a plan to do it.
38.11: You will say to yourself, “With my army I will attack the people of this land whose villages have no walls around them. I will attack people who are living quietly and who feel secure, all of them living in places that have no walls, no gates, and no bars.
38.12: I will take away everything valuable that they own. I will attack the towns that soldiers had destroyed but where people are living once again. I will attack these people who have come back from many people groups and who have acquired livestock and other possessions. I will attack these people who live at this significant place in the world.” \
38.13: The people of Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and its bold traders will say to you, “You are certainly coming in order to steal everything valuable. You have certainly gathered your army together in order to carry off silver and gold, to seize livestock and other possessions, and to take away a huge amount of goods.”’ \
38.14: So then human, prophesy to Gog. Say to him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘At that time, when my people Israel are living peacefully, you will certainly notice it.
38.15: Then you will come from your home in the far north, and many peoples will come with you. They will be an enormous army, and all of them will be riding horses.
38.16: Your army will attack my people Israel, and your soldiers will be so many that they will spread over the whole land like a cloud. This will happen in a far future time. Gog, I will bring you to attack my land so that the people groups will come to know me. They will watch what I do to you, and in that way I will show them that I am holy.’ \
38.17: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Do not think that you are the person about whom I spoke long ago through my servants, the prophets of Israel, when for many years during that time they prophesied that I would bring someone to attack the people of Israel.
38.18: No, what will happen at the time when you, Gog, step onto the ground belonging to Israel, is this: I will become furious. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
38.19: Because I am fiercely protective of my people and because I am extremely angry, I solemnly promise that at that time there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.
38.20: The fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the wild animals, every creature that crawls on the ground, and every person living on the earth will tremble before me. Mountains will fall down, cliffs will collapse, and walls everywhere will fall to the ground. \
38.21: I will make men fight against you, Gog, on all my mountains. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. Every one of your soldiers will attack his fellow soldier with his sword.
38.22: I will punish you by causing a deadly disease among you and by causing many people to die violently. I will send heavy rain, hailstones, and burning sulfur down on you and on your troops and on the many peoples who are with you.
38.23: In that way I will show that I am great and that I am holy, and people of many nations will come to know who I am as they watch. They will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God.’” \

39.1: Yahweh also said to me, “Now you human, prophesy against Gog. Tell him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Gog, you who are the most important ruler over Meshech and Tubal, be aware that I am your enemy!
39.2: I will turn you around and drive you along. I will bring you up from the far north, and I will send you to fight on the mountains of Israel.
39.3: Then I will knock your bow out of your left hand and make your arrows drop from your right hand. \
39.4: You and all of your troops and all of the peoples who come with you will die on the mountains of Israel. I will give your dead bodies as food to birds of every kind that feed on flesh and to the wild animals.
39.5: You will die out in the open country, because I myself have said that it will happen. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
39.6: I will cause fires to burn throughout the land of Magog and among the people who live in the lands along the seacoasts and who think that they are safe there. Then they will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God. \
39.7: I will clearly display that I am the powerfully holy one among my people Israel, and I will never again allow people to have any reason to say that I am not powerfully holy. Then the people of other nations will know that I, Yahweh, am the all-powerful God, the holy one who lives among the people of Israel.
39.8: Mark my words, the time when these things will happen is certainly coming. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. It is the time that I have spoken to you about. \
39.9: Then the people who live in the cities of Israel will go out, gather up the weapons, and burn them. They will burn the small shields and the large shields, the bows and the arrows, the clubs that soldiers carry in their hands, and the spears. They will use those weapons to make fires for seven years.
39.10: They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut wood in the forests, because they will make their fires with those weapons. They will actually be taking plunder from the people who came to plunder them! That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
39.11: At that time I will give Gog a place in Israel; it will be his grave, in the Valley of the Travelers, which is east of the sea. That grave will block the people who travel through it. There the people will bury Gog and the whole crowd of soldiers who came with him, and they will call it the Valley of Hamon Gog. \
39.12: For seven months the people of Israel will be burying those dead bodies, so that the dead bodies will no longer defile the land by remaining unburied.
39.13: All of the people of the land of Israel will work together to bury them, and doing that will cause people to honor them. At that time everyone will see how glorious I am. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
39.14: At the end of the seven months, the people will appoint men to continue to work at this task. Those men will travel through the land searching for and burying the bodies of the invaders that still lie on the ground, in order to make the land acceptable to me again.
39.15: As those men travel through the land, whenever any one of them sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it. When the gravediggers see the markers, they will pick up the bones and bury them in the Valley of Hamon Gog.’
39.16: ( There is also a city named Hamonah.) ‘In this way the people will make the land acceptable to me again.’ \
39.17: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say to you human: Call out to every kind of bird and to every wild animal. Tell them that I say, ‘Gather yourselves together from everywhere and come to the feast that I am preparing for you. I will slaughter a great many people on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat men’s flesh and drink their blood.
39.18: You will eat the flesh of mighty soldiers, and you will drink the blood of the rulers of the nations. I will slaughter them as though they were the rams and lambs and goats and bulls that people sacrifice, all of them like the well-fed animals from the region of Bashan. \
39.19: At the sacrifice that I am preparing for you, you will eat fat until you are completely full, and you will drink blood until you can drink no more.
39.20: It will be as though you are eating at a table that I have prepared for you. You will eat all you want of the flesh of horses and of the men who ride them, of mighty soldiers and of every kind of fighting man. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’ \
39.21: I will show the people of many nations how glorious I am, and all of those people will see how I have justly punished them.
39.22: Starting at that time and then always afterward, the people of Israel will know that I, Yahweh, am their all-powerful God. \
39.23: The people of many nations will also know that I banished the people of Israel from their land because they sinned, that is, they acted unfaithfully toward me. So I refused to help them and instead let their enemies capture them and kill very many of them.
39.24: I punished them in the way that they deserved, because they had become disgusting to me and had rebelled against me. So I refused to help them. \
39.25: Therefore this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: Now I will make the descendants of Jacob prosperous again, and I will act mercifully toward all of the people of Israel. I will work passionately to keep anyone from having a reason to say that I am not powerfully holy.
39.26: When the people of Israel are living safely in their own land with no one making them afraid, then they will feel ashamed of the disgraceful things that they did previously and of all of the ways that they had acted unfaithfully toward me.
39.27: I will bring them back from among the other peoples. Yes, I will definitely gather them from the lands of their enemies to their own land. When I do that for them, then the people of many nations will understand that I am powerfully holy. \
39.28: Then the people of Israel will know that I, Yahweh, am their all-powerful God, because I sent them into exile among the people groups and I will gather them back into their own land again. I will not leave any of them in those places any longer.
39.29: I will never again refuse to help them after I generously give my Spirit to the people of Israel. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.” \

40.1: It was 24 years after the Babylonians forcibly removed us Israelites from our land. It was 13 years after the Babylonians conquered the city of Jerusalem. It was the tenth day of the first month. On that day, Yahweh acted powerfully toward me and took me there.
40.2: God did this in a vision. He took me to the land of Israel and he set me down on a very high mountain. On the south side of the mountain were buildings that together looked like a city. \
40.3: Then Yahweh took me to those buildings. There, I saw a man! He was standing at an entrance, and he shone like bronze. He was holding a linen rope and a stick for measuring things.
40.4: The man told me, “Human, God took you to this place so that you would learn things. So, you must look at, listen to, and think carefully about everything that I will show you. Later, you must tell the Israelites everything that you learned.” \
40.5: Now the stick that the man was holding was for measuring things using longer measurements than normal. It was about 3.2 meters long. Then I saw a wall that went all the way around the area where the temple building was. The man used the stick to measure the wall. It was 3.2 meters thick and 3.2 meters tall.
40.6: Then the man went to the gatehouse on the east side of the wall and climbed up its stairs. He measured the threshold. It was 3.2 meters deep.
40.7: Inside the gatehouse, there were small side rooms. They were 2.7 meters apart. Each side room was 3.2 meters deep and 3.2 meters wide. Where the gatehouse opened toward the temple building, there was an entryway. Inside the entryway, there was a threshold. It was 3.2 meters deep. \
40.8: The man measured the entryway where the gatehouse opened toward the temple building.
40.9: It was 4.3 meters deep. The walls around its opening were 1.1 meters deep. That was what the man measured for the entryway where the gatehouse opened toward the temple building.
40.10: Inside the gatehouse on the east side, there were three small side rooms on each side of the hallway. Each of them was the same size. The walls around each of their openings were the same size. \
40.11: The man measured the open space for the gatehouse’s door. It was 5.4 meters wide. The gatehouse’s hallway was seven meters wide.
40.12: In front of each small side room, there was a half wall. Each half wall was 54 centimeters wide, and each small side room was 3.2 meters on each side.
40.13: Then the man measured along the top of the gatehouse from the back of one small side room to the back of the small side room on the other side of the hallway. It was 13.5 meters wide. \
40.14: He measured all the walls around the gatehouse’s openings, ending at the walls around the opening to the courtyard. They were 32.4 meters high.
40.15: He measured from the front of the gatehouse, where people entered, to the end of the entryway on the inside. It was 27 meters.
40.16: There were niches on the inside of the small side rooms, on the walls around their openings, and in the entryway all around the inside of the gatehouse. Carvings of palm trees were on the walls around the gatehouse’s openings. \
40.17: Then the man had me walk into the courtyard that was between the outer wall and the inner wall. I saw stone flooring all the way around the inside of the outer wall. I also saw 30 rooms. Their back walls were the outer wall, and they opened to the inside onto the stone flooring.
40.18: The stone flooring stretched out into the courtyard as far as each of the gatehouses did. This flooring was lower than the courtyard inside the inner wall.
40.19: The man measured from the inner side of the gatehouse in the outer wall that was lower than the courtyard inside the inner wall. He measured to the outside of the gate that led to the courtyard that was inside the inner wall. It was 54 meters long. That was what the man measured for the gatehouse on the east side. Then, we went to the gatehouse on the north side. \
40.20: He measured the gatehouse on the north side of the outer wall. He measured how deep and how long it was.
40.21: It had three small side rooms on each side of the hallway, walls around its openings, and entryway. They were all exactly the same size as the ones in the gatehouse on the eastern side. The gatehouse was 27 meters long and 13.5 meters wide. \
40.22: It had niches, an entryway, and carvings of palm trees. They were all exactly the same size as the ones in the gatehouse that faced east. People had to walk up seven steps to enter the gatehouse. Its entryway was on its inner side.
40.23: Just as there was on the east side, on the north side there was a gatehouse through the inner wall in line with the outer gatehouse. The man measured from this inner gate to the gate through the outer wall on the north side. It was 54 meters. \
40.24: Then, the man had me walk to the south side of the courtyard. There, I saw the gatehouse on the south side of the wall. He measured the walls around its openings and its entryway. They were the same size as the ones in the other gatehouses.
40.25: There were niches all around the inside of the gatehouse and its entryway. They were the same as the niches in the other gatehouses. This gatehouse was 27 meters long and 13.5 meters wide. \
40.26: People had to walk up seven steps to enter the gatehouse. Its entryway was on its inner side. On each of the walls around its openings there were carvings of palm trees.
40.27: On the south side there was a gatehouse through the inner wall. The man measured from this inner gate to the gate through the outer wall on the south side. It was 54 meters. \
40.28: Then the man had me walk into the courtyard that was inside the inner wall. We went through the gatehouse on the south side of the inner wall. He measured that gatehouse. It was exactly the same size as the other gatehouses.
40.29: It had small side rooms, walls around its openings, and an entryway. They were exactly the same size as the ones in the other gatehouses. There were niches all around the inside of the gatehouse and its entryway. The gatehouse was 27 meters long and 13.5 meters wide.
40.30: The entryways to each of the gates through the inner wall were 13.5 meters long and 2.7 meters wide.
40.31: The south gatehouse’s entryway opened to the courtyard between the inner and outer walls. Carvings of palm trees were on the walls around its openings. People had to walk up eight steps to enter it. \
40.32: Then the man had me walk to the east side of the courtyard that was inside the inner wall. He measured the gatehouse there. It was exactly the same size as the other gatehouses.
40.33: It had small side rooms, walls around its openings, and an entryway. They were exactly the same size as the ones in the other gatehouses. There were niches all around the inside of the gatehouse and its entryway. The gatehouse was 27 meters long and 13.5 meters wide.
40.34: Its entryway opened to the courtyard between the inner and outer walls. Carvings of palm trees were on each of the walls around its openings. People had to walk up eight steps to enter it. \
40.35: Then the man had me walk to the gatehouse on the north side of the inner wall. He measured it. It was exactly the same size as the other gatehouses.
40.36: It had small side rooms, walls around its openings, and an entryway. There were niches all around the inside of the gatehouse. The gatehouse was 27 meters long and 13.5 meters wide.
40.37: Its entryway opened to the courtyard between the inner and outer walls. Carvings of palm trees were on each of the walls around its openings. People had to walk up eight steps to enter it. \
40.38: There was a room next to each inner gatehouse. Each had a door that opened into the entryway of that gatehouse. That was where people washed their wholly burned sacrifices.
40.39: Inside the north gatehouse’s entryway, there were two tables on each side of the hallway. People killed the animals for their wholly burned sacrifices, purifying sacrifices, and restoring sacrifices on those tables. \
40.40: Outside the north gatehouse’s entryway, next to its front walls, there were two tables on each side of the steps that went up to the entryway.
40.41: So, there were four tables on each side of the gatehouse. People killed animals for sacrifices on those eight tables. \
40.42: Someone had shaped stones to make the four tables inside the gatehouse on which people killed their wholly burned sacrifices. Each table was 81 centimeters long, 81 centimeters wide, and 54 centimeters tall. People put on these tables the tools they used to kill the wholly burned sacrifices and any other kind of sacrifice.
40.43: People also put on those tables the meat from their sacrifices. There were shelves on the inside walls of the entryway structure all around. Each shelf was 8 centimeters deep. \
40.44: Within the courtyard that was inside the inner wall and its gatehouses, there were two rooms. One room was next to the north gatehouse. Its door opened to the south. The other room was next to the east gatehouse. Its door opened to the north.
40.45: The man told me, “The room whose doors open to the south is for the priests who guard the temple building. \
40.46: The room whose doors open to the north is for the priests who guard the altar. All those priests are descendants of Zadok. They are the only Levites who can approach Yahweh to serve him.”
40.47: Then he measured the courtyard inside the inner walls. It was square, 54 meters long on each side. There was an altar in front of the temple building. \
40.48: Then the man had me walk into the temple building’s entryway. He measured the walls around the gateway opening. They were 2.7 meters thick on each side. The gateway opening was 7.6 meters across. The front walls that spanned from the gateway to the side walls were 1.6 meters wide on each side.
40.49: The entryway was 10.8 meters wide and 6.5 meters deep. People had to walk up stairs to enter it. There were two large posts just outside the walls around the entryway’s opening, one on each side. \

41.1: Then the man had me walk into the Holy Place. He measured the walls around its opening. They were 3.2 meters thick on each side.
41.2: The opening into the Holy Place was 5.4 meters across. The walls that spanned from the opening to the side walls were 2.7 meters wide on each side. Then the man measured the Holy Place. It was 21.6 meters long and 10.8 meters wide. \
41.3: Then the man went into the inner room. He measured the walls around its opening. They were 1.1 meters thick. The opening into the room was 3.2 meters across. The walls that spanned from the opening to the side walls were 3.8 meters wide on each side.
41.4: He measured that inner room, which was at the far end of the Holy Place. It was 10.8 meters long and 10.8 meters wide. He told me, “This room is the Most Holy Place.” \
41.5: Then the man measured the wall for the temple building. It was 3.2 meters thick. There were rooms along the outside of the temple building’s wall on its north, south, and west sides. Each of these side rooms was 2.2 meters wide.
41.6: There were 30 side rooms around the temple building, and each one had two more side rooms directly above it. There were ledges all around the temple building’s wall to support these rooms. That way, the temple building wall itself did not support these rooms.
41.7: The side rooms were deeper at the top than at the bottom all around the temple building. So, the outside of the temple building was wider at the top than at the bottom. There were steps that went around and up the inside of the front side rooms. That way, people could walk up to the highest room from the lowest room through the middle room. \
41.8: I noticed that the temple building stood on a platform on all sides. The part of the platform that the side rooms stood on was 3.2 meters high.
41.9: The outer wall for the side rooms was 2.7 meters thick. Outside the side rooms that were along the outer wall of the temple building, between them \
41.10: and the rooms that were further away from the temple building, there was an open space 10.8 meters wide around the whole temple building.
41.11: There were two doorways into the side rooms. One faced north and one faced south. They opened into an open space at the edge of the platform. This open space was 2.7 meters wide all around the temple building. \
41.12: On the west side of the courtyard that went around the temple building, there was another building. Its wall was 2.7 meters thick all the way around. The inside of the building was 38 meters east to west and 49 meters north to south.
41.13: Then the man measured the temple building from east to west. It was 54 meters long. He measured the courtyard on the western side of the temple building, the other building, and the other building’s walls from east to west. In total, they were 54 meters long.
41.14: The courtyard on the east side of the temple building was 54 meters from north to south. \
41.15: The man measured the other building, the one that was on the west side of the western courtyard. He included its walkways on each side. It was 54 meters from north to south. As for the Holy Place, the Most Holy Place, and the entryway out into the courtyard,
41.16: those three rooms all had thresholds, niches, and walkways all around. Starting at the threshold, there were long, thin pieces of wood covering the walls, niches, and walkways all around, from the floor to the niches. The niches had coverings over their openings.
41.17: The long, thin pieces of wood covered everything from above the entrance into the temple building to the Most Holy Place. They covered all the walls, inside and outside the temple building, all the way around. Each piece of wood was exactly the same size. \
41.18: Workmen had carved cherubs and palm trees on the pieces of wood. There was always one palm tree between two cherubs. Each cherub had two faces.
41.19: A human face looked toward the palm tree on one side. A lion’s face looked toward the palm tree on the other side. Workmen had carved this pattern on the walls all around the temple building.
41.20: From the floor to the top of the entrance, including the walls of the Holy Place, workmen had carved the cherubs and palm trees. \
41.21: The sides of the door frame into the Holy Place had faces at right angles to each other. The door frames into the Most Holy Place were exactly the same as those.
41.22: In the Holy Place, there was a wooden altar. It was 1.6 meters high and 1.1 meters long and wide. Its corner pieces, base, and sides were wooden. Then the man told me, “This is a table. It is in Yahweh’s presence.”
41.23: The entrance into Holy Place and the entrance into the Most Holy Place each had two sets of doors.
41.24: Each of the two sets of doors at each entrance had two panels that swung on hinges. \
41.25: Workmen had carved cherubs and palm trees on the sets of doors into the Holy Place. They were just like the carvings on the temple building’s walls. There was a wooden covering over the area just outside the entryway into the temple building.
41.26: On the two walls that spanned from the entryway opening to its sidewalls, there were niches and carvings of palm trees. The rooms on the outside of the temple building also had coverings. \

42.1: Then the man had me walk out into the courtyard that was between the inner and outer walls. We went through the gate on the north side of the inner walls. He led me to some rooms. These rooms were next to the courtyard and building that were on the west side of the temple building. The rooms were on the north side of that courtyard and building.
42.2: All together, those rooms were 54 meters from east to west and 27 meters from north to south. There was an entrance on their north side.
42.3: The courtyard that was 10.8 meters wide to the west of the temple building was on the southeast side of those rooms. The stone flooring around the inside of the outer walls was on the northwest side of those rooms. The outside of the rooms had walkways that divided them into three stories. \
42.4: On the north side of the rooms, there was a walkway 5.4 meters wide and 54 meters long. The rooms’ doors opened on the north side.
42.5: The rooms on the third story were narrower north to south than the rooms on the lower stories. That is because the walkways above the first and second stories used space that would have been part of the rooms on the floor above.
42.6: So, there were three stories of rooms. However, although the rest of the rooms in both courtyards had large posts, these rooms did not. Because of that, the highest story was narrower than the middle story, which was narrower than the lowest story. \
42.7: Along the north side of the rooms, at the north edge of the walkway, there was a low wall. It was 27 meters long from east to west.
42.8: That low wall was only 27 meters long because the rooms along the outer wall were 27 meters deep. So, the length of the room next to the western outer wall and the length of the low wall added up to the length of these rooms that were nearer to the Holy Place. They were 54 meters long.
42.9: On the ground floor of these rooms, there was an entryway on the eastern side. A person could enter from the courtyard between the inner and outer walls \
42.10: where the low wall began. There were more rooms next to the courtyard and building that were on the west side of the temple building. These rooms were on the south side of that courtyard and building.
42.11: There was a walkway on the south side of those rooms, just like the one on the north side of the northern rooms. They were exactly the same size as the northern rooms, and they had the same measurements, exits, and entrances.
42.12: Those rooms had entrances that opened to the south. The entrance to the walkway was like those entrances. A person could enter it at the eastern end of the walkway and the low wall that was on the south side of the walkway. \
42.13: Then the man told me, “The northern and southern rooms that are next to the courtyard to the west of the temple building are sacred. Because they are sacred, the priests who approach Yahweh set the most sacred offerings there, including grain offerings, purifying offerings, and restoring sacrifices. They also eat the most sacred offerings there.
42.14: Now the clothes that the priests wear when they are serving as priests in sacred areas are also sacred. So, when the priests are ready to leave those sacred areas, they must first leave their clothes in the rooms to the north or the south of the temple building. When they have changed into other clothes, they can go into the courtyard between the inner and outer walls and to where the rest of the people are.” \
42.15: The man had now completed measuring everything inside the temple area. Next, he had me walk outside the temple area through the gatehouse on the east side. Then, he measured the area all around the outside. \
42.16: He measured the east side with the stick for measuring things. It was 270 meters long.
42.17: He measured the north side with the stick for measuring things. It was 270 meters long.
42.18: He measured the south side with the stick for measuring things. It was 270 meters long.
42.19: Then he went to the west side and measured it with the stick for measuring things. It was 270 meters long. \
42.20: In summary, the man measured the temple area on all four sides. There was a wall all the way around it, and it was 270 meters long on each side. This wall divided the sacred area from the ordinary area outside it. \

43.1: After that, the man had me walk to the gatehouse that went through the outer eastern wall.
43.2: Then suddenly, I saw the glorious, brilliant light coming from the God of Israel! It was moving toward us from the east and lit up the ground around it. His voice was as loud as crashing waves. \
43.3: What I saw looked exactly like what I saw previously when God arrived to destroy Jerusalem. It also looked exactly like what I saw previously when I was at the Kebar River. So, I threw myself face down on the ground.
43.4: The glorious, brilliant light coming from Yahweh went through the gatehouses on the east side of the temple area. It arrived at the temple building.
43.5: Then a wind lifted me up and carried me to the courtyard inside the inner walls. Then I saw that the glorious, brilliant light coming from Yahweh filled the temple building. \
43.6: The man who had measured everything was standing next to me. Then I heard someone inside the temple building speaking to me.
43.7: Then Yahweh said to me, “Human, this is where I will rule as king. I will make myself present here with the Israelites forever. The Israelite people and their kings will no longer cause people to dishonor me, the holy God. They used to do that when they worshiped other gods, performed rituals to appease their dead kings after they died,
43.8: and built houses against the temple walls. They did disgusting things, which made people dishonor me, the holy God. So, I was angry with them and destroyed them. \
43.9: At this time, they must stop worshiping other gods and performing rituals to appease their dead kings. Then, I will make myself present here with them forever. \
43.10: As for you, human, describe the temple area to the Israelites. That will shame them for what they have done wrong. Have them study carefully how I have designed it.
43.11: Suppose that everything wrong that they have done does shame them. In that case, tell them about the design of the temple building and where everything in it is. Tell them about its exits and entryways. Tell them about the rules and instructions for it. Write it all down for them. Then, they must do everything that I have instructed them to do. \
43.12: Listen to this very important instruction concerning the temple building. The area all around the top of this mountain is very sacred. \
43.13: Here is what the altar’s parts measure, using longer measurements than normal. Each unit of measure is 54 centimeters long. There is a gutter around the base of the altar. It is 54 centimeters deep and 54 centimeters across. There is a rim all around the outside of the gutter. It is 23 centimeters high. What follows are the parts that make up the altar’s bottom part.
43.14: There are side walls from the bottom of the gutter to a ledge 1.1 meters above the ground. The ledge is 54 centimeters deep. There are more side walls from this lower ledge to a higher ledge 2.2 meters above the lower ledge. This higher ledge is also 54 centimeters deep. \
43.15: The flat area for burning things is 2.2 meters above the higher ledge. There are four projections upward, one from each of the four corners of the flat area.
43.16: The flat area for burning things has corners that are right angles. Each side is 6.5 meters long.
43.17: The highest ledge has corners that are right angles. Each side is 7.6 meters long. Around the flat area for burning things is a gutter. At the outer edge of the gutter, there is a rim that is 27 centimeters high. The gutter is 54 centimeters deep. There are steps to the altar on the east side.” \
43.18: Then Yahweh told me, “Human, I, the Lord Yahweh, say this, ‘These are the instructions about the altar. When workmen finish building the altar, you must follow these instructions before the Israelites regularly offer wholly burned sacrifices on it and splatter blood on it.
43.19: You, Ezekiel, must provide the priests with a young bull as a purifying sacrifice. Those priests are descendants of Zadok. They are the Levites who can approach me to serve me. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
43.20: After slaughtering the bull and catching its draining blood in a bowl, you must smear some of the blood on the four projections from the top of the altar, the four corners of the highest ledge, and the rim that goes around that ledge. In this way, you will cleanse the altar and make it pure.
43.21: Then, you must retrieve the dead body of the bull that you used for the purifying sacrifice. You must have someone burn the body outside the sacred area in the proper place. \
43.22: The next day you must offer a male goat as a purifying sacrifice. It must be completely healthy. The priests must cleanse the altar with it in the same way they cleansed the altar with the bull.
43.23: At that point, you and the priests have completed cleansing the altar. After that, you must offer a young bull and a ram. They must be completely healthy.
43.24: You must bring them to my presence. The priests must sprinkle salt on them. Then, they must offer them as a wholly burned sacrifice to me. \
43.25: On each of the next five days, you must offer a male goat as a purifying sacrifice. The priests must also offer a young bull and a ram. Those animals must be completely healthy.
43.26: In summary, for seven days in total the priests must make the altar pure. As they do that, they will dedicate it to me.
43.27: Once that is done, from the eighth day after they began and onward, the priests will offer you Israelites’ wholly burned sacrifices and fellowship sacrifices on that altar. Then, I will be happy with you. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’” \

44.1: Then the man took me back to the gatehouse that opened through the outer wall on the eastern side. Someone had closed it securely.
44.2: Yahweh told me, “I, Yahweh, the God whom you Israelites worship, passed through this gatehouse. So, this gatehouse must stay closed at all times. No one may open it or pass through it.
44.3: The man who leads the Israelites is the only one who may go inside this gatehouse. He may eat special food there in my presence. He must both enter and exit the gatehouse only through the entryway.” \
44.4: Then the man had me walk through the gatehouse on the north side of the inner wall. We walked to the area in front of the temple building. When I looked at Yahweh’s temple building, I saw that the glorious, brilliant light coming from Yahweh filled it! So, I threw myself face down on the ground.
44.5: Then Yahweh told me, “Human, watch, listen, and think carefully about all of the instructions and rules concerning my temple building that I am about to tell you. Think carefully about the temple building’s entryway and all of the exits from the temple area. \
44.6: Here is what I want you to tell the Israelites, who openly defy me. ‘This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say to you. You Israelites have done too many disgusting things!
44.7: You invited people who were not Israelites into my temple area while you were offering fat and blood from sacrifices to me. No one had circumcised those people, and they did not want to obey me. So, they defiled my temple building. When you Israelites did many disgusting things like that, you disobeyed the agreement that I made with you. \
44.8: You did not guard the sacred things that belong to me. Instead, you had people who were not Israelites guard my temple area.
44.9: Here is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say. All people who are not Israelites are not allowed to enter the temple area. No one has circumcised those people, and they do not want to obey me. That rule applies to all people who are not Israelites but who live among the Israelites. \
44.10: However, as for the descendants of Levi, they stopped worshiping and obeying me. They did that when the rest of the Israelites did what was wrong by no longer worshiping me and instead worshiping other gods. So, I will punish the Levites for what they did wrong.
44.11: They must serve in the temple area. They must guard the gatehouses that lead to the temple building, and they must take care of the temple building. They are the ones who must kill the animals that the Israelites offer as wholly burned sacrifices or as any other kind of sacrifice. They must help the rest of the Israelites.
44.12: Here is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. The Levites helped the rest of the Israelites worship other gods. They caused the Israelites to do what was wrong. So, I have solemnly promised that I will punish them for what they did wrong. \
44.13: They must not come near me to serve me as priests, and they must not come near any of my holy things or the most holy offerings. They must feel ashamed because they acted shamefully and did detestable things, and accept that I must punish them for what they did.
44.14: Instead, I will assign them to take care of the temple and to do all of the work that anyone needs to do in it. \
44.15: However, the priests who are Levites and who descend from Zadok faithfully served in my temple when the rest of the people of Israel abandoned me. So they are the only ones who may come near to me to serve me. I permit only them to stand before me and present to me the fat and the blood of the sacrifices. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
44.16: I permit only them to enter my temple, and I permit only them to come near my altar to serve me. I assign them to do everything that has to do with serving me. \
44.17: Whenever they enter the gateways of the inner courtyard, they must put on linen clothes. They must not wear anything made of wool while they serve within the gateways of the inner courtyard or inside the temple.
44.18: They must wear linen cloths wrapped around their heads and they must wear linen undergarments around their private parts. They must not wear anything that makes them perspire. \
44.19: Before they go back out to the outer courtyard where the people gather, they must take off the clothes in which they were serving and leave those clothes in the holy rooms. Then they must put on other clothes, so that they do not endanger the people by touching them with the holy clothes. \
44.20: These priests must not shave their heads, and they must not let their hair grow long. They must always keep the hair on their heads trimmed.
44.21: No priest may drink wine when he goes into the inner courtyard.
44.22: Priests must not marry widows of men who were not priests or women whose husbands have divorced them. They may marry only virgins who descend from the people of Israel, or widows whose husbands were priests. \
44.23: The priests must teach my people the difference between what is holy and what is ordinary, and they must show them the difference between things that are acceptable to me and things that are not acceptable to me.
44.24: When there are disputes between people, the priests are the ones who must judge what is right and wrong. They must settle the dispute according to my laws. They must obey my regulations concerning all of the festivals that I have appointed, and they must keep my Sabbath days holy. \
44.25: As a general rule, a priest must not go near a corpse, because touching a corpse would defile him. However, he may become defiled in order to touch the dead body of his father or his mother, his son or his daughter, his brother, or a sister who has never married.
44.26: A priest who has become defiled must perform the rituals to make himself acceptable to me again. After he has made himself acceptable again, he must wait seven days before serving in the temple.
44.27: Then on the day when he goes into the inner courtyard of the Holy Place to serve me there, he must present an offering to take away his sin. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
44.28: The work of serving me will be my gift for the priests; I myself will provide everything that they need. You people must not give them any property in Israel, because they must rely on me.
44.29: The priests are the ones who will eat the offerings that people bring of grain, the offerings that take away people’s sin, and the offerings that remove people’s guilt. Everything in Israel that the people dedicate completely to me will belong to the priests. \
44.30: The best of all of the first crops that you people harvest and every gift that you present to me will belong to the priests. You must also give to the priest the first batch of your dough. If you do that, I will bless everyone who lives in your homes.
44.31: The priests must not eat any bird or animal that died on its own or that wild animals killed. \

45.1: When you divide the land of Israel among the tribes and give each tribe its permanent share, you must set apart one portion of the land and present it to me, Yahweh, as a holy gift. That portion will be 13.5 kilometers long and 10.6 kilometers wide. The whole area inside its borders will be holy.
45.2: Inside that area, a square plot 270 meters on each side will be for the temple, and an open space 27 meters wide will surround that plot on every side. \
45.3: Inside the holy area you must measure off a section 13.5 kilometers long and 5.3 kilometers wide. The sanctuary, the most holy place of all, will stand in the square plot which will be inside that section.
45.4: That section will be the holy portion of the land, and it will belong to the priests, the ones who serve in the sanctuary and who come near to me, Yahweh, to serve me. There they will build their houses, and part of it will be a holy place for the sanctuary building.
45.5: The other section that is 13.5 kilometers long and 5.3 kilometers wide will belong to the descendants of Levi who serve at the temple. That land will be their own property, and they can build cities to live in there. \
45.6: Alongside the holy portion that you set apart, you must give an area 2.7 kilometers wide and 13.5 kilometers long for the city. It will belong to all the people of Israel.
45.7: The ruler will have land in two areas, on either side of the area set aside for the holy portion and the city portion. On the west of these portions, his land will begin where those portions end and extend westward to the sea. On the east side of these portions, his land will begin where those portions end and extend eastward to the eastern border of the country. So from west to east his land will be just as long as the territory that each tribe receives, from the sea to the eastern border, with the holy and city portions dividing it in the middle. \
45.8: That land will be the ruler’s own property in Israel. Then the rulers whom I appoint will no longer oppress my people. Instead, they will let the people of Israel have the rest of the land, and each tribe will receive its own share. \
45.9: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say! I am angry with you, rulers of Israel, because of what you have been doing! Stop acting violently and oppressing the people. Instead, do what is right and govern my people justly. Stop taking land from my people! That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
45.10: You must use accurate scales, accurate baskets for measuring dry things, and accurate containers for measuring liquids.
45.11: The basket that you use for dry things and the container that you use for liquids must hold the same amount. Each of them must hold one tenth of a homer, that is, 22 liters, because a homer holds 220 liters. You must base both measures on the homer.
45.12: Your shekel must weigh 20 gerahs (11 grams ). Combining 20 shekels, 25 shekels, and 15 shekels must equal one mina. \
45.13: This is the offering that you must present to the ruler of Israel; out of every 60 liters of wheat that you harvest, you must give one liter, and out of every 60 liters of barley that you harvest, you must give one liter.
45.14: This is the rule about olive oil; out of every 100 liters that you produce, you must give 1 liter. You may do this by giving the tenth part of a bath out of every homer, since a bath is the tenth part of a homer.
45.15: You must also give one sheep out of every 200 sheep from the flocks that graze in the well-watered pastures of Israel. The priests will use all these things for the grain offerings, for the sacrifices that they burn completely, and for the offerings that the people make to maintain fellowship with me, so that I will forgive the people for their sins. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
45.16: All of the people of the land must give these things to the ruler in Israel.
