45.17: From these things the ruler then must provide what the priests need for the sacrifices that they burn completely, for the grain offerings, and for the drink offerings. He must do this at the festivals, at the celebrations of the new moon, and on the Sabbath days — at every time that I have appointed for the people of Israel to worship. He himself must provide what the priests need for the offerings that take away sin, the grain offerings, the sacrifices that the priests burn completely, and the offerings that maintain fellowship with me, so that I will forgive the people of Israel for their sins. \
45.18: This is also what I, the Lord Yahweh, say! On the first day of the first month of the year, you must take a young bull that has no defects, and you must offer it in order to make the sanctuary acceptable to me.
45.19: The priest must take some of the blood from that sacrifice that takes away sin and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge that is around the altar, and on the posts of the gateway into the inner courtyard.
45.20: You must do the same thing on the seventh day of that month on behalf of anyone who sins without intending to sin and anyone who sins because he does not know that what he does is a sin. In this way you will make the temple acceptable to me. \
45.21: On the fourteenth day of the first month of the year you must begin to celebrate the Passover festival. It is a festival that lasts a full week of seven days. During this festival you must not eat bread that has yeast in it.
45.22: On that first day of the Passover festival the ruler must provide a bull as an offering to take away his own sin and the sin of all of the people of the land. \
45.23: On each of the seven days of the festival he must provide seven bulls and seven rams that have no defects, and the priests will burn them completely as sacrifices to me, Yahweh. He must also provide a male goat each day as an offering to take away sin.
45.24: For the grain offerings the ruler must provide 22 liters of flour with each bull and 22 liters with each ram, and 3.7 liters of olive oil with every 22 liters of flour. \
45.25: Then on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when the people celebrate the Festival of Shelters, the ruler must provide on each of the seven days exactly what I have just told you to provide at the Passover festival; the same offerings to take away sin, the same sacrifices that the priests burn completely, the same grain offerings, and the same amount of olive oil. \

46.1: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say. The gateway of the inner courtyard of the temple that faces east must remain closed during the six days each week when people work. But on every Sabbath day the gatekeeper must open it, and on every day when the new moon appears he must open it.
46.2: The ruler must enter through the porch of that gateway from the outer courtyard, and he must stand beside the gatepost there. While he stands there, the priests must offer the animal that he brings for them to burn completely and the animals that he brings for the offering to maintain fellowship with me. Then he must bow down at the threshold of the gateway to worship me, and after that he may go out. The gatekeeper must leave that gateway open until evening. \
46.3: On the Sabbath days and on the days when the new moon appears, the ordinary people of the land must also gather at the entrance of that gateway and bow down before me there to worship me.
46.4: On each Sabbath day the ruler must bring six lambs and one ram for the priests to burn completely as an offering to me, Yahweh. All of those animals must have no defects at all.
46.5: Along with the ram he must bring 22 liters of flour as a grain offering, and along with the lambs he may bring as much flour as he chooses to give. With every 22 liters of flour he must bring 3.7 liters of olive oil. \
46.6: On each day when the new moon appears, he must bring a young bull from those in the herd that have no defects. He must also bring six lambs and a ram. All of those animals must have no defects at all.
46.7: As a grain offering he must provide 22 liters of flour with the bull and 22 liters of flour with the ram, and with the lambs he may provide as much flour as he can afford. With every 22 liters of flour he must provide 3.7 liters of olive oil.
46.8: Whenever the ruler comes in, he must enter through the porch of the gateway, and when he goes out, he must go out by that same way. \
46.9: Whenever the ordinary people come before me to worship me at the festivals that I have appointed, whoever enters through the north gateway must go out through the south gateway, and whoever enters through the south gateway must go out through the north gateway. None of them may turn around and leave through the gateway that he entered. Each of them must walk straight ahead and go out through the opposite gateway.
46.10: The ruler must be among the people. He must go in when they go in, and he must go out when they go out. \
46.11: At the festivals and at the other times that I have appointed, the grain offering must be 22 liters of flour with the bull and 22 liters of flour with the ram, and with the lambs the ruler may bring as much flour as he chooses to give. With every 22 liters of flour he must bring 3.7 liters of olive oil.
46.12: Sometimes the ruler may want to bring to me, Yahweh, an offering that I have not required of him, whether an animal for the priests to burn completely or animals for an offering to maintain fellowship with me. When he wants to do that, the gatekeeper must open for him the gateway on the east side of the temple. Then he must present those offerings just as he does on a Sabbath day. Then after he goes out, the gatekeeper must close the gateway behind him. \
46.13: Every morning one of you must provide a lamb that is one year old and that has no defects at all, and the priests must burn it completely as an offering to me, Yahweh, for that day.
46.14: Every morning one of you must also provide a grain offering to go with that lamb. The offering must be 3.7 liters of flour, and 1.2 liters of olive oil to moisten the flour. This rule about this grain offering to me, Yahweh, does not end.
46.15: So every morning the priests must offer the lamb, the grain offering, and the olive oil, and they must burn that offering completely. They must do this every day. \
46.16: This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say. If the ruler gives some of his land as a gift to one of his sons, that land will belong to that son permanently. The son’s descendants will receive it after him, and they will own it permanently.
46.17: However, if the ruler gives some of the land that I have allotted to him to one of his servants, that servant may keep it only until the year when everyone must return property to the family that first owned it. Then the land will belong to the ruler again. Only the ruler’s sons can inherit the ruler’s land.
46.18: The ruler must not seize any of the land that any of the people own and thus force any of them from his own property. The ruler must give to his sons only land that he already owns himself, so that no one among my people has to leave the land that belongs to him.’” \
46.19: Then the man who was showing me the temple area brought me through the entrance at the side of the gateway into the holy rooms that are on the north side of the temple. They are the rooms that belong to the priests. There I saw a place at the west end of those rooms.
46.20: He said to me, “This is the place where the priests must boil the meat of the offerings that remove people’s guilt and the offerings that take away people’s sin, and where they must bake the flour from the grain offerings. They must do all of that here so that they do not carry those holy things out into the outer courtyard where people might touch them and thus become a holy sacrifice themselves.” \
46.21: Then the man brought me out to the outer courtyard and led me past its four corners. I saw that in each corner of that courtyard there was a smaller courtyard.
46.22: Each of the four small courtyards in the four corners of the outer courtyard had walls around it. Each one was 21.5 meters long and 16 meters wide. All four of them were the same size.
46.23: Around the inside of each of those four small courtyards was a stone ledge. Underneath the ledges, all the way around, workers had built places for cooking fires.
46.24: The man said to me, “These are the kitchens where the men who serve in the temple must boil the meat of the sacrifices that the people bring.” \

47.1: Then the man brought me back to the entrance of the temple. I saw water there! It was flowing out from under the doorway of the temple and running toward the east, because the temple faced east. The water was flowing down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
47.2: Then the man led me out through the north gate and around the outside to the outer gate that faces east. There I saw water trickling out on the south side of that gate. \
47.3: As the man walked on toward the east, he held a measuring line in his hand. He measured off 540 meters from the temple and then led me through water there that came up to my ankles.
47.4: Then he measured off another 540 meters and led me through water that came up to my knees. Then he measured off another 540 meters and led me through water that came up to my waist.
47.5: Then he measured off another 540 meters, and at that place the water had become a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen so deep that anyone who wanted to get to the other side would have to swim. No one could walk through it. \
47.6: Then he said to me, “Human, think carefully about what you have seen.” Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
47.7: As I came back, I was surprised to see that there were very many trees that had grown up on both sides of the river.
47.8: Then he said to me, “This water flows out toward the eastern region and down into the valley of the Arabah, and then it enters into the Salt Sea. When this water that flows out from the temple reaches that sea, it will make the salty water there fresh. \
47.9: This will happen; wherever this river flows, every kind of living creature that swarms in the water will live. There will be very many fish, because this water will come there and make the salty water fresh. Everywhere the river flows, every creature will live.
47.10: This will also happen; fishermen will stand along the shore of that sea. All the way around from En Gedi to En Eglaim they will spread out their fishing nets. There will be very many kinds of fish there, as many kinds as there are in the Great Sea. \
47.11: But the swamps and the pools along the shore of the Salt Sea will stay salty, so that people can get salt from them.
47.12: Fruit trees of every kind will grow along both banks of the river. Their leaves will never wither, and they will never stop producing fruit. They will produce fresh fruit every month, because the water that makes them grow flows out from the sanctuary. People will eat their fruit, and they will use their leaves to heal sick people.” \
47.13: This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “I will tell you the boundaries of the land that you must divide among the twelve tribes of Israel as their permanent possession. The descendants of Joseph will receive two shares of it and the Levites will not receive any.
47.14: You must divide it so that each other tribe receives a fair share. I solemnly promised your ancestors that I would give them this land, and now this land will become yours to own permanently. \
47.15: These will be the boundaries of the land. On the north, the border will begin at the Great Sea and extend along the road to Hethlon, past Lebo, and on to Zedad,
47.16: and then to Hamath, Berothah, and Sibraim, which is between the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath, and on to Hazer Hattikon, which is on the border of Hauran.
47.17: So the northern boundary will extend from the Great Sea to Hazar Enon. The boundary will be north of the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath will be north of the boundary. That will be the northern boundary of the land. \
47.18: On the east side, the boundary will extend south between the territories of Hauran and Damascus and then turn west to the Jordan River, which separates Gilead from the land of Israel. It will follow the Jordan River south to the eastern salt sea. You must measure it from the northern border down to the eastern sea and to Tamar. That will be the eastern border.
47.19: On the south side, the boundary will extend from Tamar to the springs at Meribah Kadesh, and then along the streambed at the border of Egypt out to the Great Sea. That will be the southern boundary.
47.20: On the west, the Great Sea will be the boundary. This boundary will extend from the southern boundary to a point opposite Lebo Hamath. That will be the western boundary. \
47.21: You must divide this land among yourselves, giving a share to each of the tribes of Israel.
47.22: This is important; you must divide this land so that it becomes a permanent possession for yourselves and also for the foreigners who live among you and who have had children among you. You must consider those foreigners to be just like native Israelites. They must receive a share of land along with you, among the tribes of Israel.
47.23: You must give each foreigner a share of land within the territory of the tribe among whom he has been living. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \

48.1: These are the names of the tribes and the shares of land that each of them will receive. The northern border of the country will run alongside the road to Hethlon, then on to Lebo Hamath and to Hazar Enan, which lies on the border of Damascus, with the region of Hamath to the north. The tribe of Dan will receive one share of land there, and it will extend from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea.
48.2: South of Dan’s land, the tribe of Asher will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea.
48.3: South of Asher’s land, the tribe of Naphtali will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea. \
48.4: South of Naphtali’s land, the tribe of Manasseh will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea.
48.5: South of Manasseh’s land, the tribe of Ephraim will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea.
48.6: South of Ephraim’s land, the tribe of Reuben will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea.
48.7: South of Reuben’s land, the tribe of Judah will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea. \
48.8: South of Judah’s land, extending from the eastern border of the country west to the Great Sea, is where the tract of land that you must set apart as a holy gift will be. It will measure 13.5 kilometers from north to south, and from east to west it will be as long as one of the shares that the tribes receive. The sanctuary will be in the middle of it.
48.9: Inside that tract of land you must set apart a portion of land as a holy gift for me, Yahweh. It will be 13.5 kilometers east to west and 5.4 kilometers north to south. \
48.10: This holy tract of land will belong to the priests. It will be 13.5 kilometers along its northern side, 5.4 kilometers along its western side, 5.4 kilometers along its eastern side, and 13.5 kilometers along its southern side. My sanctuary will be in the middle of it.
48.11: It will belong to the priests who are descendants of Zadok, the ones whom I set apart to serve me. They faithfully performed the duties that I assigned to them, and they did not abandon me when the rest of the people of Israel abandoned me, as the other descendants of Levi did.
48.12: So when you divide the land, this special tract will belong to the priests, and it will be inside of the larger holy gift that you set apart from the land. It will be the most holy part of all, and it will be next to the land that belongs to the descendants of Levi. \
48.13: The descendants of Levi will receive land alongside the territory of the priests, and their land will be 13.5 kilometers long and 5.4 kilometers wide. So each of these two tracts will be 13.5 kilometers in length ( east to west ) and 5.4 kilometers in width ( north to south ).
48.14: The descendants of Levi must never sell any of this land, and none of them may trade it away or transfer it to anyone else, because it is the best part of the land and it belongs to me, Yahweh, as something holy. \
48.15: The remaining strip of land, which will be 2.7 kilometers wide and will be alongside the tract that is 13.5 kilometers long, will not be holy. Ordinary people will use it, building their houses there and keeping their animals in the pastureland there, and the city will be in the middle of it.
48.16: These will be the measurements of the city: 2.4 kilometers along its northern side, 2.4 kilometers along its southern side, 2.4 kilometers along its eastern side, and 2.4 kilometers along its western side. \
48.17: Pastureland will surround the city as a border: This border will be 135 meters wide on the north, 135 meters wide on the south, 135 meters wide on the east, and 135 meters wide on the west.
48.18: What remains of the portion of land for the ordinary people that is alongside the holy tract will be 5.4 kilometers to the east of the city and 5.4 kilometers to the west of the city. In that way this portion will be the same length as the holy tract. This portion will be where people who work in the city will grow their food. \
48.19: Workers from all of the tribes of Israel will come to work in the city, and they will farm that land.
48.20: The entire area that you set apart will be a square measuring 13.5 kilometers on each side. This includes the holy tract that you will set apart as well as the property that belongs to the city. \
48.21: The land on the eastern and western sides of the square that contains the holy tract and the property belonging to the city will belong to the ruler. On the east, his land will begin at the eastern edge of that square, and will also be 13.5 kilometers wide from north to south. His land will extend to the eastern border of the country. On the west, his land will begin at the western edge of that square and will also be 13.5 kilometers wide from north to south. It will extend from there westward to the Great Sea. These two areas for the prince, with the holy tract and the temple in between them, will be as long east to west as the shares of land that the tribes receive.
48.22: The land of the ruler will be between the territory of the descendants of Judah on the north and the territory of the descendants of Benjamin on the south, and the property of the descendants of Levi and the property of the city will be in the middle of the land for the ruler. \
48.23: The rest of the tribes will also each receive one share of land that extends from the eastern border of the country to the Great Sea in the west. South of the holy tract, the tribe of Benjamin will receive one share.
48.24: South of Benjamin’s land, the tribe of Simeon will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country to the Great Sea in the west.
48.25: South of Simeon’s land, the tribe of Issachar will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country to the Great Sea in the west.
48.26: South of Issachar’s land, the tribe of Zebulun will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country to the Great Sea in the west. \
48.27: South of Zebulun’s land, the tribe of Gad will receive one share, extending from the eastern border of the country to the Great Sea in the west.
48.28: The southern border of Gad’s land will be the southern border of the country. It will go from Tamar to the waters of Meribah Kadesh, and then along the streambed at the border of Egypt westward to the Great Sea.
48.29: That is how you must divide the land among the tribes of Israel, and each tribe will own its share permanently. Those will be the portions that each tribe receives. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. \
48.30: The following will describe the exits from the city, beginning with the gates on the city’s northern side, which will measure 2.4 kilometers.
48.31: You will name the gates of the city after the tribes of Israel. On the north side there will be three gates: name one gate for Reuben, name one gate for Judah, and name one gate for Levi.
48.32: The eastern side will measure 2.4 kilometers, and it will also have three gates: name one gate for Joseph, name one gate for Benjamin, and name one gate for Dan. \
48.33: The southern side will measure 2.4 kilometers, and it will also have three gates: name one gate for Simeon, name one gate for Issachar, and name one gate for Zebulun.
48.34: The western side will measure 2.4 kilometers and it will have three gates: name one gate for Gad, name one gate for Asher, and name one gate for Naphtali.
48.35: The distance all around the city will be 9.6 kilometers. From that day on, the name of the city will be “Yahweh Is There.”
